method: 35-agent workflow: 17 subsystem auditors -> adversarial verifier per unit -> completeness critic; every finding re-verified against code + pinned gbrain source

units.unit_summary: Audited the 7 shared-infra files (types.ts, judge.ts, eval-adapter-config.ts + test, llm-budget.ts, identity.ts, synthetic-corpus-loader.ts) plus their consumers (multi-adapter.ts, shootout-driver.ts, cat5/9/14 runners) and the gbrain v0.47.6.0 library surface. Import verification: 'gbrain/pglite-engine' exists in the export map and every PGLiteEngine method identity.ts calls (connect, initSchema, putPage, upsertChunks, searchKeyword, disconnect) exists with compatible signatures; '@anthropic-ai/sdk' is a declared dependency. 12 findings: 5 majors — (1) judge.ts weightedMean averages over the judge-returned criteria instead of the rubric, so omitted criteria silently drop out of the denominator and duplicates double-count, feeding directly into pass/fail verdicts; (2) recallAtK counts duplicate page_ids so recall can exceed 1.0; (3) precisionAtK divides by returned-list length instead of k, rewarding adapters that return fewer docs; (4) sanitizeQuery forwards acceptable_variants (acceptable answer phrasings) and known_failure_modes to adapters, contradicting the sealed-qrels blinding contract (latent — no committed queries populate the field yet); (5) synthetic-corpus-loader walks with unsorted readdirSync and then slices the first 10/10/5 entities, making the derived query set filesystem-order dependent. Minors: judge verdict parsed then unconditionally discarded despite a documented ±0.5-band trust rule, pricing comment mislabels dollars as cents (constants verified correct at $1/$5 per MTok Haiku 4.5), systemPromptVersion config accepted but never used or recorded, dead _manifest.json filter. 3 improvements: exclude gold-less queries from P/R means instead of scoring 0, add retry-attempt accounting to JudgeResult, make CORPUS_DIR cwd-independent. Clean files: llm-budget.ts (semaphore check-and-increment is synchronous on the event loop, so no overspend race; env parsing NaN-guarded), eval-adapter-config.ts and its test, and identity.ts (its page-level dedup is redundant with searchKeyword's internal dedup but harmless; metrics denominators correct).

findings.verifier_note: Exactly as claimed. weightedMean (lines 241-252) iterates the judge's scores, not the rubric; a missing criterion vanishes from numerator and denominator, a duplicated criterion_id is weighted twice, and an invented id gets fallback weight 1 via `?? 1` (line 247). parseToolUse line 274 only checks Array.isArray(obj.scores) with no coverage/duplicate validation, so no retry fires on partial scores (a fully empty array yields totalWeight=0 -> overall 0 -> fail, but any partial subset skews the mean). Downstream confirmed: verdict derived from this mean at judge.ts:389 and cat9-workflows.ts:199 does `pass: judgeResult.verdict === 'pass'`. The 'typically inflating' direction is speculative, but the coverage defect and pass/fail impact are real.
findings.title: weightedMean silently drops rubric criteria the judge omits and double-counts duplicates
findings.evidence: weightedMean iterates the judge's returned scores, not the rubric: `for (const s of scores) { const w = weightById.get(s.criterion_id) ?? 1; totalScore += s.score * w; totalWeight += w; }` (lines 246-250). If the judge omits a rubric criterion, that criterion vanishes from both numerator and denominator, so the overall score is a mean over only the criteria the judge chose to score (typically inflating it, since judges tend to omit criteria they cannot verify). If the judge returns the same criterion_id twice its weight is counted twice, and an invented criterion_id not in the rubric gets fallback weight 1 and pollutes the mean. parseToolUse (line 274) only checks `Array.isArray(obj.scores)` — an empty or partial scores array passes validation, so no retry fires. Downstream this directly flips pass/fail: cat9-workflows.ts line 199 does `pass: judgeResult.verdict === 'pass'` and the verdict is derived from this mean (judge.ts line 389).
findings.suggested_fix: After parsing, validate coverage: require exactly one score per rubric criterion (reject extras/duplicates/missing) and treat a mismatch like a malformed response (retry, then judge_failed). Alternatively, iterate the rubric in weightedMean, treating a missing criterion as score 0 while keeping its weight in totalWeight, and ignore criterion_ids not in the rubric.
findings.status_note: judge weightedMean iterates rubric; coverage mismatch = malformed->retry->judge_failed

findings.verifier_note: Code is exactly as quoted (lines 267-272): hits increments per RankedDoc, not per unique page_id, so relevant={a}, docs=[a,a] yields 2.0. The Adapter contract nowhere forbids duplicate page_ids, and identity.ts:100-102 shows engine results are chunk-grained and need explicit page dedup. Callers confirmed at multi-adapter.ts:349 and shootout-driver.ts:200. One qualification: all four current in-repo adapters happen to dedup to page level (hybrid aggregates page-best score, vector/bm25 score per doc), so the inflation is latent for current runs; it is live for any new adapter that returns chunk-level results, which the contract permits.
findings.title: recallAtK counts duplicate page_ids multiple times; recall can exceed 1.0
findings.evidence: Line 270-272: `let hits = 0; for (const d of topDocs) if (relevant.has(d.page_id)) hits++; return hits / relevant.size;`. hits increments once per RankedDoc, not per unique relevant page. An adapter that returns the same page_id at two ranks within top-K (easy with chunk-level results; identity.ts lines 100-102 dedups explicitly because engine results are chunk-grained) gets hits=2 for one relevant page: relevant={a}, docs=[a,a] gives recall 2/1 = 2.0. Both multi-adapter.ts:349 and shootout-driver.ts:200 sum this per query into mean_recall_at_k, so duplicate-returning adapters get silently inflated recall.
findings.suggested_fix: Count unique matched ids: `const matched = new Set<string>(); for (const d of topDocs) if (relevant.has(d.page_id)) matched.add(d.page_id); return matched.size / relevant.size;`. Apply the same unique-hit counting to precisionAtK so a duplicated relevant doc does not count twice in the numerator.
findings.status_note: metrics.ts unique-id recall; types.ts delegates

findings.verifier_note: Exactly as claimed: `return hits / topDocs.length` (line 263) with early return 0 on empty. The contract explicitly allows short lists (types.ts:222-224 'adapters are free to return fewer than k'), and the docstring at line 257 says 'fraction of top-k'. This is active, not latent: grep-only.ts and vector.ts only emit docs with score > 0, so they routinely return fewer than TOP_K=5, and multi-adapter.ts:348 / shootout-driver.ts:199 average these values across adapters, systematically favoring terse result lists.
findings.title: precisionAtK divides by returned-list length, not k — rewards adapters that return fewer docs
findings.evidence: Line 258-264: `const topDocs = topK(docs, k); if (topDocs.length === 0) return 0; ... return hits / topDocs.length;`. The Adapter contract explicitly allows short lists (types.ts lines 222-224: 'adapters are free to return fewer than k'). An adapter returning 1 doc that is relevant scores P@10 = 1.0, while an adapter returning 10 docs with the same single relevant hit scores 0.1. The docstring (line 257) says 'fraction of top-k', and the cross-adapter comparison in multi-adapter.ts:348 averages these values, so the metric systematically favors low-recall, terse adapters.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the standard P@k denominator: `return hits / k;` (with unique-hit counting per the recallAtK fix). If the 'precision over returned' variant is wanted too, expose it as a separately named function so scorecards label it correctly.
findings.status_note: precision /k

findings.verifier_note: Line 140 copies acceptable_variants (and line 141 known_failure_modes) into PublicQuery; PublicQuery = Omit<Query,'gold'> (line 127) strips only gold. acceptable_variants is documented at line 110 as 'for LLM-judged outputs', i.e. acceptable answer phrasings, which contradicts the stated anti-cheat purpose at lines 117-125. The comment at line 124-125 does say 'PublicQuery keeps every field EXCEPT gold', so the mechanical behavior is documented, but the blinding intent is undermined regardless. Confirmed latent: grep of eval/data finds no committed query populating acceptable_variants or known_failure_modes. The reference-sharing claim is also accurate: out.tags/out.acceptable_variants alias the caller's arrays despite the 'sever the reference chain' comment at lines 130-132 (which only addresses the object/gold key).
findings.title: sanitizeQuery leaks acceptable_variants (gold-adjacent answer variants) to the system under test
findings.evidence: Line 140: `if (q.acceptable_variants !== undefined) out.acceptable_variants = q.acceptable_variants;`. Query.acceptable_variants is documented at line 110 as 'for LLM-judged outputs' — i.e. acceptable phrasings of the expected answer. PublicQuery = Omit<Query,'gold'> (line 127) strips only the `gold` field, so an adapter receives the acceptable answer variants (and `known_failure_modes`, line 141) verbatim, contradicting the sealed-qrels contract stated at lines 117-125 ('the sanitized copy strips the gold field entirely, so an adapter cannot ... cheat'). Currently latent — no committed query data in eval/data populates acceptable_variants — but any future Tier-judged query set silently un-blinds every adapter. Additionally, the copied arrays are shared by reference despite the 'sever the reference chain' comment at line 130, so an adapter can mutate q.tags/q.acceptable_variants seen by the scorer.
findings.suggested_fix: Change PublicQuery to also omit acceptable_variants and known_failure_modes, and drop lines 140-141 from sanitizeQuery. Copy remaining array fields (`out.tags = [...q.tags]`) to actually sever references.
findings.status_note: PublicQuery shrunk to {id,text,as_of_date}

findings.verifier_note: walk() at line 38 iterates readdirSync(dir) with no sort (Node applies none), and syntheticQueries() takes order-dependent prefixes: companies.slice(0,10) at line 67, concepts.slice(0,10) at line 82, meetings.slice(0,5) at line 97, plus sequential synq IDs from the counter. Which pages land in each slice depends on raw directory iteration order, which varies across filesystems/machines (ext4 htree hash order is seeded per-filesystem), so two clones can run different query subsets. The deterministic-seed framing is in the doc comment at lines 45-52 (finding cited 48-51; trivially off). Header says the loader feeds Cat 18/20/25/26/27/29.
findings.title: Unsorted readdirSync makes the derived query set filesystem-order dependent
findings.evidence: walk() at line 38 iterates `readdirSync(dir)` with no sort, and syntheticQueries() selects machine-order-dependent subsets: `companies.slice(0, 10)` (line 67), `concepts.slice(0, 10)` (line 82), `meetings.slice(0, 5)` (line 97). Node's readdirSync returns entries in raw directory order (hash order on ext4, insertion-dependent on APFS), so two clones of the same committed corpus can run different Q1/Q2/Q3 query subsets across Cat 18/20/25/26/27/29, making reported numbers non-reproducible across machines despite the deterministic-seed framing in the header comment (lines 48-51).
findings.suggested_fix: Sort the directory listing in walk(): `for (const entry of readdirSync(dir).sort())`, or sort `pages` by slug at the end of loadSyntheticV1() before returning.
findings.status_note: sorted walk

findings.verifier_note: Exactly as claimed. The comment at lines 386-388 describes a ±0.5 alignment band, but line 389 is just `const computedVerdict = verdictFromScore(overall)` and the return uses `verdict: computedVerdict` (line 393, finding said 392; return statement starts at 391). parsed.verdict is required by the tool schema (enum at line 156, required at line 159), validated at line 275, and never read afterward. No band check or disagreement logging exists anywhere in the file.
findings.title: Judge's verdict is parsed and validated, then unconditionally discarded, contradicting the stated ±0.5-band contract
findings.evidence: The comment at lines 386-388 says 'Trust the model's verdict only if it aligns with the computed score (within ±0.5 band). Otherwise use the computed verdict', but the code is just `const computedVerdict = verdictFromScore(overall);` and the return at line 392 uses `verdict: computedVerdict` — `parsed.verdict` (required by the tool schema at line 156 and validated at line 275) is never read after parsing. No band check exists, and a large model/threshold disagreement is not surfaced anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Either implement the documented band logic (and log/record a `verdict_disagreement` flag when |model verdict band - computed band| exceeds it), or delete the misleading comment, drop `verdict` from the required tool schema, and document that the 3.5/2.5 thresholds are the sole verdict source.
findings.status_note: verdict policy comment matches code

findings.verifier_note: Line 111 comment reads '(2026-04 cents per 1M tokens)' above PRICE_INPUT_PER_M = 1.0 / PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_M = 5.0. Verified against current Anthropic pricing: Claude Haiku 4.5 is $1.00/MTok input and $5.00/MTok output (USD). priceOf() at lines 301-303 divides by 1_000_000, so cost_usd fields are correct in dollars; only the comment's unit is wrong by 100x. Minor doc bug, correctly scoped by the finding.
findings.title: Pricing comment says 'cents per 1M tokens' but constants are dollars per 1M
findings.evidence: Line 111-113: `// Haiku 4.5 pricing (2026-04 cents per 1M tokens). const PRICE_INPUT_PER_M = 1.0; const PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_M = 5.0;`. Haiku 4.5 is $1.00/MTok input and $5.00/MTok output, so the constants and priceOf() (line 302, divides by 1_000_000) correctly yield USD — the unit in the comment is wrong by 100x and invites a bad 'fix' that would corrupt every cost_usd field.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comment to '// Haiku 4.5 pricing (USD per 1M tokens: $1 input / $5 output).'
findings.status_note: pricing comment dollars

findings.verifier_note: Grep across the entire eval tree finds exactly one occurrence of systemPromptVersion: the declaration at judge.ts:102. scoreAnswer() (lines 333-402) reads config.client/model/maxTokens/systemPrompt but never systemPromptVersion; it selects nothing, is not sent to the model, and JudgeResult has no field carrying it. Dead config surface exactly as described.
findings.title: JudgeConfig.systemPromptVersion is accepted but never used or recorded
findings.evidence: Line 101-102 declares `systemPromptVersion?: string` with the comment 'System prompt version for reproducibility. Pinned via gold/personalization-rubric.json', but scoreAnswer() (lines 333-402) never reads config.systemPromptVersion — it does not select a prompt, is not sent to the model, and is not echoed into JudgeResult. Runs claiming a pinned prompt version have no record of which prompt actually graded them.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the field, or record it (plus the resolved model id) in JudgeResult so report JSON captures exactly which judge prompt/model produced each verdict.
findings.status_note: systemPromptVersion recorded in JudgeResult

findings.verifier_note: Line 22 `if (!file.endsWith('.md')) return;` rejects everything not ending in '.md', so line 23's `if (file.endsWith('_manifest.json')) return;` can never be true for a path that survived line 22. Dead code, harmless but exactly as described.
findings.title: Dead _manifest.json filter — unreachable after the .md extension check
findings.evidence: Line 22 `if (!file.endsWith('.md')) return;` already rejects every non-.md file, so line 23 `if (file.endsWith('_manifest.json')) return;` can never execute (a path cannot end in both '.md' and '_manifest.json').
findings.suggested_fix: Delete line 23, or if manifest files can be named `*_manifest.json.md`/similar, reorder the checks so the manifest exclusion runs first.
findings.status_note: dead filter removed

findings.verifier_note: Code fact exact: types.ts:268-269 returns 0 when relevant.size === 0, and multi-adapter.ts:347 does `new Set(q.gold.relevant ?? [])`, so such a query would contribute a hard 0 to both means. Important qualification: the consequence is fully latent today. Every current query source guarantees non-empty relevant — multi-adapter buildQueries() and shootout-driver buildRelationalQueries() both `continue` when expected.length === 0, and the only committed subset (brainbench-cat13-embedder-subset.json) has zero empty relevant_chunk_ids arrays. Fair as the design-hazard improvement it is labeled, not an active scoring error.
findings.title: recallAtK returns 0 for empty relevant sets, silently deflating mean recall for gold-less queries
findings.evidence: Line 268-269: `if (relevant.size === 0) return 0;`. multi-adapter.ts line 347 builds `new Set(q.gold.relevant ?? [])`, so any query whose gold uses expected_answer/abstention shapes instead of `relevant` contributes a hard 0 to both mean_precision_at_k and mean_recall_at_k rather than being excluded — an unweighted drag on the average that looks like adapter failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Have scorers skip queries with no `gold.relevant` (exclude from the denominator) or assert non-empty relevant sets at load time; if the helper must handle it, return NaN or a sentinel the caller filters instead of 0.
findings.status_note: NaN for empty gold + callers exclude

findings.verifier_note: Exactly as claimed. JudgeResult's only flakiness signal is fallback_used (line 91), set true only when both attempts fail (line 381); the success path always returns fallback_used: false (line 400). Attempt 2's tokens and cost are folded into the totals (lines 357-361) with no record that a retry occurred, so a doubled cost_usd is unexplainable from the report JSON.
findings.title: Retry accounting invisible: a success on attempt 2 is indistinguishable from a clean first-attempt success
findings.evidence: JudgeResult only carries `fallback_used` (line 91), which is true only when both attempts fail (line 381). When attempt 1 is malformed and attempt 2 succeeds (lines 356-362), the doubled input_tokens/cost are folded into the totals but nothing records that a retry happened, so judge flakiness rates cannot be monitored across a run and cost-per-probe anomalies are unexplainable from the report JSON.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `attempts: 1 | 2` field to JudgeResult (set from whether attempt2 ran) so runners can aggregate a judge malformed-response rate alongside fallback_used.
findings.status_note: JudgeResult.attempts

findings.verifier_note: Line 11: `const CORPUS_DIR = join(process.cwd(), 'eval/data/synthetic-v1')` at module scope. loadSyntheticV1() -> walk() -> readdirSync(CORPUS_DIR) throws ENOENT when the process cwd is not the repo root, before any useful error, and there is no override parameter. Consequence is real for the six consuming runners named in the file header (Cat 18/20/25/26/27/29). Fair minor improvement.
findings.title: CORPUS_DIR resolved from process.cwd(), breaking runners invoked outside the repo root
findings.evidence: Line 11: `const CORPUS_DIR = join(process.cwd(), 'eval/data/synthetic-v1');` — evaluated at module load. Running any of the six consuming runners (cat18/18b/20/29 etc.) from a different working directory throws ENOENT in readdirSync before any useful error message, and the constant cannot be pointed at a fixture dir in tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve relative to the module: `join(import.meta.dir, '../data/synthetic-v1')` (Bun), and optionally accept an override parameter in loadSyntheticV1(dir?) for tests.
findings.status_note: corpus dir import.meta relative

units.unit_summary: Audited the adapters-queries unit: 3 baseline adapters (grep-only BM25, vector-only, hybrid-no-graph), the Claude-Sonnet agent adapter, tier 5/5.5 query corpora, the query validator, and the PDF loader, cross-checking every gbrain import against the v0.47.6.0 checkout. Core retrieval math is sound: BM25 (Lucene IDF variant, k1/b defaults, deterministic tie-breaks) and cosine ranking are correct, ranks are 1-based per the Adapter contract, gold is structurally sealed from adapters (sanitizePage/sanitizeQuery), and all gold slugs plus the one exact-date gold verify against the world-v1 corpus. Found 6 bugs and 3 improvements. Most impactful: (1) the agent loop's 'rate_limit_exhausted' stop_reason is unreachable — exhausted retries throw and, since Cat 8/9 run probes under an uncaught Promise.all, one sustained 429 aborts the whole category run; (2) computeBrainFirstOrdering mislabels turn-cap/no-answer runs as 'answer_before_brain' and structurally cannot detect real answer-before-brain ordering, corrupting Cat 8's per-probe compliance labels; (3) the 80 hand-authored tier 5/5.5 queries are schema-validated in CI but never executed by any runner despite the file header claiming they fill a scorecard column. Smaller issues: vector.ts imports a nonexistent EMBEDDING_MODEL symbol (receipt field silently undefined), the hybrid adapter's documented limit knob is dead, q5-0004 ships answer-string gold that can only score 0, the tier getters' 'defensive copy' still shares gold.relevant references, cosine silently truncates on dim mismatch (with a test enshrining it), and the validator checks gold shape for only 2 of 8 output types.

findings.verifier_note: Verified. The while loop (lines 208-234) exits only via break-on-success (line 223) or throw (line 232): the retry guard `isRateLimitError(err) && attempt < maxRetries - 1` (line 226) means attempt maxes at maxRetries-1, so the while condition never goes false with response null; the final failed attempt throws. `if (!response)` at line 235 is dead code for any maxRetries >= 1 (default 3 at line 82). Callers confirmed: cat8-skill-compliance.ts line 222 and cat9-workflows.ts line 179 both `await runAgentLoop` inside identical runConcurrently helpers (cat8 line 201, cat9 line 123: `results[idx] = await fn(items[idx])`, no try/catch), and both use `await Promise.all(workers)`, so one worker's throw rejects the whole category run. The header comment (line 20-21) and the AgentRunResult type (line 70) both promise the rate_limit_exhausted behavior that never fires.
findings.title: stop_reason 'rate_limit_exhausted' is unreachable; exhausted retries throw and kill the whole Cat 8/9 run
findings.evidence: In the retry loop (lines 208-234), the only exits are `break` on success or `throw err` at line 232: the catch retries only when `isRateLimitError(err) && attempt < maxRetries - 1` (line 226), so the final failed attempt throws instead of falling through. The dead-code guard `if (!response) { stopReason = 'rate_limit_exhausted'; ... }` (lines 235-239) can never execute with the default maxRetries=3. Callers do not catch: cat8-skill-compliance.ts line 222 and cat9-workflows.ts line 179 await runAgentLoop inside runConcurrently workers (`results[idx] = await fn(items[idx])`, no try/catch), so one probe hitting sustained 429s rejects Promise.all and aborts the entire category run.
findings.suggested_fix: In the catch, on a rate-limit error at the last attempt, set `response = null` and `break` (or restructure to `if (isRateLimitError(err)) { attempt++; if (attempt >= maxRetries) break; await sleep(...); continue; } throw err;`) so the documented 'rate_limit_exhausted' stop_reason actually fires and the probe is recorded as failed instead of crashing the run.
findings.status_note: Retry loop in runAgentLoop (eval/runner/adapters/claude-sonnet-with-tools.ts:337-364) now breaks with response=null when the final attempt is rate-limited, so the documented stop_reason 'rate_limit_exhausted' fires and the probe completes gracefully instead of rejecting Promise.all. Non-rate-limit e

findings.verifier_note: Verified. Lines 411-417 are exactly as quoted: 'answer_before_brain' is returned only when brainCalls > 0 AND finalAnswerProduced is false, i.e. the loop hit turnCap with zero answers (finalAnswerRecorded is set true only in the no-tool-call break at lines 273-284). So a run that never answered is labeled as having answered before consulting the brain. Conversely no transcript-order check exists: assistant text emitted in turn 1 alongside a tool call is discarded (only the final no-tool turn's text becomes final_answer), so pre-written answers are always labeled 'brain_before_answer'. Consumption confirmed: cat8-skill-compliance.ts line 233 copies the label into per-probe output and scoreBrainFirst (lines 119-121) treats only 'brain_before_answer' as compliant, so turn-cap runs are silently folded into non-compliance under a misleading label.
findings.title: computeBrainFirstOrdering mislabels turn-cap runs as 'answer_before_brain' and can never detect real answer-before-brain ordering
findings.evidence: Lines 411-417: `if (brainCalls.length === 0) return 'no_brain_calls'; if (finalAnswerProduced) return 'brain_before_answer'; return 'answer_before_brain';`. The 'answer_before_brain' branch fires only when the loop hit turnCap WITHOUT producing any answer (finalAnswerRecorded=false), so a run with zero answers is reported as "answered before consulting the brain". Conversely, real ordering is never checked: the loop (lines 273-285) only records a final answer on a no-tool-call response, so a model that writes its complete answer as text in turn 1 alongside a throwaway `search` call is classified 'brain_before_answer'. Cat 8 copies this label into per-probe output (`brain_first: result.brain_first_ordering`, cat8-skill-compliance.ts line 233).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the third branch to something honest like 'no_final_answer' (and treat it as non-compliant in scoreBrainFirst), or compute ordering from the transcript: compare the turn_index of the first BRAIN_READ_TOOLS tool_call against the first assistant turn containing substantive answer text.
findings.status_note: computeBrainFirstOrdering gained a distinct 'no_answer' label for brainCalls>0 with no final answer, and real answer-before-brain is now detected from trace order: substantive assistant text (>=80 chars, SUBSTANTIVE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS) emitted in a tool-calling turn while zero brain reads have executed

findings.verifier_note: Verified. Lines 145-146 destructure EMBEDDING_MODEL from a dynamic import of 'gbrain/embedding', which maps to /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src/core/embedding.ts (package.json exports line 20). That module (gbrain v0.47.6.0 per its package.json) exports getEmbeddingModelName (line 117), getEmbeddingDimensions (line 122), EMBEDDING_COST_PER_1K_TOKENS, and multimodal re-exports, but no EMBEDDING_MODEL; repo-wide grep of /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src finds only unrelated DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL / GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL identifiers in other modules. Destructuring a missing property from a dynamic-import namespace yields undefined (no link-time error, unlike static named imports), so state.embeddingModel (documented at line 64-65 as the reproducibility receipt) is undefined in default non-shootout mode.
findings.title: Imports nonexistent EMBEDDING_MODEL from gbrain/embedding; receipt field is silently undefined
findings.evidence: Line 145-146: `const { EMBEDDING_MODEL } = await import('gbrain/embedding'); embeddingModel = EMBEDDING_MODEL;`. gbrain v0.47.6.0's src/core/embedding.ts exports `getEmbeddingModelName()` and `getEmbeddingDimensions()` but no `EMBEDDING_MODEL` constant (verified via grep across /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src: zero hits). Destructuring a missing property from a dynamic-import namespace yields `undefined` at runtime under bun (no typecheck), so the state's `embeddingModel` field, documented as "Embedding model used (for scorecard reproducibility card)" (line 65), is always undefined in default (non-shootout) mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with `const { getEmbeddingModelName } = await import('gbrain/embedding'); embeddingModel = getEmbeddingModelName();` (or hardcode 'openai:text-embedding-3-large' to match the configureGateway call at line 109).
findings.status_note: vector.ts no longer destructures the nonexistent EMBEDDING_MODEL from 'gbrain/embedding'. It statically imports getEmbeddingModel from 'gbrain/ai/gateway' (verified to exist in gbrain v0.47.6.0 at src/core/ai/gateway.ts line 824, exported via the './ai/gateway' package export) and reads the live con

findings.verifier_note: Verified exactly. Lines 38-40 document `limit?: number` with 'Defaults to 20'; init() reads _config.shootout only and returns `{ engine } satisfies HybridNoGraphState` at line 125 (HybridNoGraphState at lines 33-35 has no limit field); query() hardcodes `const limit = 20;` at line 156. A caller passing { limit: 50 } silently gets 20 and query() has no path to the config value.
findings.title: HybridNoGraphConfig.limit is documented but never used; query() hardcodes limit=20
findings.evidence: Lines 38-40 document `limit?: number` ("Top-K results requested from hybridSearch. Defaults to 20"), but init() never stores the config in state (`return { engine } satisfies HybridNoGraphState`, line 125) and query() hardcodes `const limit = 20;` at line 156. A caller passing `{ limit: 50 }` silently gets 20; the knob is unreachable by construction since query() has no access to config.
findings.suggested_fix: Store `limit` in HybridNoGraphState during init (`return { engine, limit: _config.limit ?? 20 }`) and read it in query(), or delete the config field and its doc comment.
findings.status_note: HybridNoGraphAdapter.init resolves config.limit (Number.isFinite && >= 1, floored, default 20) and stores it in HybridNoGraphState; query() reads s.limit instead of the hardcoded 20.

findings.verifier_note: Verified. q5-0004 (lines 60-69) has expected_output_type 'answer-string', gold: { relevant: [] } (line 65), and no gold.expected_answer (the Gold interface supports it, types.ts, and tier5_5-synthetic.ts uses it, e.g. q55-0048). recallAtK returns 0 when relevant.size === 0 at types.ts line 268, and precisionAtK counts zero hits against an empty set, so under the standard retrieval scorer the item can only contribute 0. Validator confirmed blind to this: validator.ts checks gold shape only for 'cited-source-pages' (lines 122-142) and 'abstention' (lines 145-154), and TEMPORAL_VERBS does not match this text, so it passes eval:query:validate clean. Only nuance: top-level acceptable_variants exists (line 66), but that is not gold.expected_answer and no judge routing exists anyway.
findings.title: q5-0004 is answer-string with empty gold: no expected_answer and relevant: []
findings.evidence: Lines 62-69: q5-0004 has `expected_output_type: 'answer-string'` but `gold: { relevant: [] }` and no `expected_answer`. If scored via the standard retrieval path, recallAtK returns 0 when relevant.size === 0 (types.ts line 268) and precision counts no hits, so the query can only ever contribute 0 regardless of system quality; an answer-string judge has no expected_answer to compare against. The validator does not catch this because it only checks gold shape for 'cited-source-pages' and 'abstention' (validator.ts lines 122-154).
findings.suggested_fix: Give q5-0004 real gold: either populate gold.relevant with the actual Series-A-2024 founder slugs from world-v1, or set gold.expected_answer and route it to the judge scorer; do not ship an eval item that structurally cannot score above 0.
findings.status_note: q5-0004 now carries real gold: gold.relevant = [people/adam-lee-19, people/carol-wilson-28, people/nina-rodriguez-18] plus gold.expected_answer for future judge routing. All three verified against world-v1 shards as _facts.role='founder' pages with explicit 2024 Series A closes on their own timeline

findings.verifier_note: Verified. Line 307 under the 'Defensive copy so callers can't mutate the canonical set' comment (line 306) spreads only the top level of gold; gold.relevant remains the same array reference, so push/splice through a returned copy mutates TIER5_FUZZY_QUERIES module state for all later callers. acceptable_variants and known_failure_modes are top-level query fields (not inside gold as the parenthetical implies) but are equally shared by reference via the shallow `{ ...q }` spread. Same pattern confirmed in tier5_5-synthetic.ts getTier5_5SyntheticQueries, lines 340-346 (finding said 341-345; getter body spans 341-345, trivially off).
findings.title: 'Defensive copy' in getTier5FuzzyQueries is shallow: gold.relevant array is still shared with the canonical set
findings.evidence: Line 307: `return TIER5_FUZZY_QUERIES.map(q => ({ ...q, gold: { ...q.gold }, tags: q.tags ? [...q.tags] : undefined }));` under the comment "Defensive copy so callers can't mutate the canonical set" (line 306). `{ ...q.gold }` copies only the top level; `gold.relevant` (and `acceptable_variants`, `known_failure_modes`) remain the same array references, so `queries[0].gold.relevant.push('x')` mutates TIER5_FUZZY_QUERIES for every later caller in the same process. Same pattern in tier5_5-synthetic.ts lines 341-345.
findings.suggested_fix: Deep-copy the array fields: `gold: { ...q.gold, relevant: q.gold.relevant ? [...q.gold.relevant] : undefined }` plus copies of acceptable_variants/known_failure_modes, or use structuredClone(q) in both getter functions.
findings.status_note: getTier5FuzzyQueries and getTier5_5SyntheticQueries now return structuredClone(q) per query (deep copy of gold.relevant, acceptable_variants, known_failure_modes, tags) instead of the shallow {...q, gold: {...q.gold}} spread.

A missing tier reads as not measured.' As shipped it is exactly not measured.
findings.title: Tier 5/5.5 query sets (80 queries) are validated but never executed by any runner
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep shows the only consumer of getAllTierQueries/getTier5FuzzyQueries/getTier5_5SyntheticQueries is eval/cli/query-validate.ts (schema validation). No benchmark runner scores them, yet tier5_5-synthetic.ts's header claims "Tier 5.5 has to exist in the scorecard for the multi-axis report to have a full column. A missing tier reads as 'not measured.'" (lines 14-16). As shipped, the tier is exactly that: not measured — carefully authored, corpus-verified gold that measures nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire getAllTierQueries() into the multi-adapter scorecard (multi-adapter.ts already has scoreOneRun + sanitizeQuery infrastructure), reporting fuzzy and externally-authored as separate scorecard rows; skip or judge-route the abstention/answer-string items that the top-K scorer cannot handle.

Empty-gold items (9 abstention/judge-only) are excluded from retrieva

findings.verifier_note: Verified as an improvement finding. Line 47 is `const n = Math.min(a.length, b.length);` under the comment 'callers upstream ensure embedder returned consistent-dim vectors' (lines 40-42), and nothing in init() or query() asserts dims. gbrain's gateway is process-global module state (gateway.ts line 463 configureGateway, line 715 'Clear every piece of module state'), so reconfiguration between one adapter's init() and query() yields silently-truncated cross-space similarities. vector.test.ts lines 40-50 confirmed: title says 'cosine returns 0 on mismatched-length vectors at the tail' while asserting `sim > 0` (the [1,1,1] vs [1,1] case actually yields 1.0). One caveat for the caller: the test's comment (lines 41-44) explicitly documents fail-soft truncation as intentional ('helps fail-soft rather than crash the benchmark'), so this is a deliberate design being critiqued, not an unnoticed defect; the finding itself acknowledges this, and its factual evidence, the misleading test title, and the mismatch with the repo's promised 'dim mismatch guards' methodology all hold.
findings.title: cosine() silently truncates on dimension mismatch (Math.min), producing plausible garbage instead of failing loud
findings.evidence: Line 47: `const n = Math.min(a.length, b.length);` with the comment "callers upstream ensure embedder returned consistent-dim vectors" — but nothing asserts it. Because gbrain's gateway is process-global (configureGateway mutates module state), any reconfiguration between init() and query() (e.g. a future runner interleaving shootout cells in one process) makes query vectors a different width/space than doc vectors, and every similarity is computed over a truncated prefix of mismatched embeddings with no error. vector.test.ts lines 40-50 even enshrines this under the misleading title "cosine returns 0 on mismatched-length vectors at the tail" while actually asserting `sim > 0`.
findings.suggested_fix: Record `dims = embeddings[0].length` in VectorOnlyState at init and throw in query() when `queryVec.length !== s.dims` (mirroring the "dim mismatch guards" the repo's methodology section promises); fix the test to assert the throw and rename it.
findings.status_note: cosine() throws on a.length !== b.length ('embedding dimension mismatch (A vs B)') instead of Math.min-truncating; the misleading fail-soft test was replaced with one asserting the throw. Per the directive, cosine never truncates.

findings.verifier_note: Verified. VALID_OUTPUT_TYPES (lines 33-42) lists 8 types; gold-shape checks exist only for 'cited-source-pages' (lines 122-142: non-empty relevant[] + slug regex) and 'abstention' (lines 145-154: expected_abstention === true). answer-string, time-qualified-answer, canonical-entity-id, contradiction-explanation, poison-flag, and confidence-score get no gold checks (the tier-5.5 author check at lines 157-165 is not a gold check). This is exactly how q5-0004 (answer-string, gold { relevant: [] }, no expected_answer, no temporal-verb match) passes eval:query:validate.
findings.title: Validator enforces gold shape for only 2 of 8 expected_output_types
findings.evidence: Lines 122-154 check gold shape only for 'cited-source-pages' (relevant[] non-empty, slug format) and 'abstention' (expected_abstention === true). 'answer-string', 'time-qualified-answer', 'canonical-entity-id', 'contradiction-explanation', 'poison-flag', and 'confidence-score' get zero gold checks, which is exactly how q5-0004 (answer-string with empty gold, tier5-fuzzy.ts line 66) passes `eval:query:validate` in CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add per-type gold checks: answer-string/time-qualified-answer require gold.expected_answer (or acceptable_variants), canonical-entity-id requires gold.expected_entity_id in slug format, time-qualified-answer additionally requires as_of_date; this makes the CI gate catch malformed contributions before they silently score 0.

units.unit_summary: Audited the BrainBench orchestrators (all.ts, multi-adapter.ts, smoke.ts, before-after.ts, shootout-driver.ts, run-skillopt-cats.sh, both shootout shell scripts, package.json) against the gbrain v0.47.6.0 checkout. All gbrain imports resolve (pglite-engine, extract, search/hybrid, import-file, ai/gateway subpaths exist with matching symbols/signatures), sanitizePage/sanitizeQuery are correctly invoked before adapter calls in both multi-adapter.ts and shootout-driver.ts, the cat13 subset gold slugs all exist in world-v1, and package.json script targets all point at real files. Found 1 critical + 8 major + 7 minor bugs and 3 improvements. Highest impact cluster is scripts/run-shootout-phase1.sh: (1) `${reranker:+VAR=val}` env-prefixes are not assignments, so all four reranker cells fail with exit 127 (verified experimentally); (2) `run_cell || handler` suspends set -e inside the function, so gbrain-eval/scoring failures fall through silently, the handler is dead code, and a partially-answered JSONL can be scored and permanently marked complete; (3) the version gate rejects the pinned gbrain 0.47.6.0; (4) GBRAIN_RERANKER_MODEL/GBRAIN_SEARCH_RERANKER_ENABLED are read nowhere in gbrain, so reranker cells would silently measure the no-rerank pipeline; (5) evaluate_qa.py is called with flags and without the reference file the published evaluator requires. Phase 2 has the same silent-failure pattern. Other majors: smoke.ts's long-haystack gate is fake (gateway embed() truncates to 8,000 chars before the provider), all.ts advertises a BRAINBENCH_N knob no subprocess Cat reads (a 'published N=10' report ran N=1), and P@5 uses a returned-length denominator that inflates short-list adapters (notably GbrainAfterAdapter's graph-only outgoing path) in the neutral head-to-head table.

findings.verifier_note: Verified lines 147-157 as quoted and reproduced in bash 5.2.15: with reranker set, `A="$r" ${r:+B="$r"} C=x env` fails with exit 127 (expansion word becomes the command name). Actually WORSE than claimed: the empty case (`r=""; A=1 ${r:+B=2} C=3 env`) also fails with `C=3: command not found` exit 127 because the removed null word still terminates the assignment prefix, so GBRAIN_SEARCH_MODE=tokenmax becomes the command name in the no-reranker cells too — all 7 cells (not 4) never invoke `gbrain eval`, and the errexit suspension (see line 172 finding) makes each still print '-> done'.
findings.title: Env-prefix built from ${reranker:+VAR=val} is not an assignment; all 4 reranker cells die with exit 127
findings.evidence: Lines 147-152: `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL="$embedder" \ GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS="$dim" \ ${reranker:+GBRAIN_RERANKER_MODEL="$reranker"} \ ${reranker:+GBRAIN_SEARCH_RERANKER_ENABLED=true} \ GBRAIN_SEARCH_MODE=tokenmax \ gbrain eval longmemeval ...`. The shell marks assignment words before expansion, so a word produced by parameter expansion is never an assignment: when reranker is set, the expansion result `GBRAIN_RERANKER_MODEL=zeroentropyai:zerank-2` becomes the COMMAND NAME. Verified in this sandbox: `A="$r" ${r:+B="$r"} C=x env` -> `bash: B=zeroentropyai:zerank-2: command not found`, exit=127. So cells A1, B1, C1, C2 (4 of 7) never invoke `gbrain eval` at all, and because errexit is suspended inside run_cell (see separate finding) the failure is swallowed and the cell still prints '-> done'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `env` with an array: `local -a envs=(GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL="$embedder" GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS="$dim" GBRAIN_SEARCH_MODE=tokenmax); [ -n "$reranker" ] && envs+=(GBRAIN_RERANKER_MODEL="$reranker" GBRAIN_SEARCH_RERANKER_ENABLED=true); env "${envs[@]}" gbrain eval longmemeval ...` (with `env` the assignments are ordinary arguments, so expansion is fine), or `export` the vars conditionally in a subshell.
findings.status_note: env(1) argv; reproduced+fixed; stub-tested

findings.verifier_note: Reproduced the semantics in bash 5.2.15: with `set -euo pipefail`, a `false` inside a function invoked left of `||` falls through to the next statement. gbrain eval (152-157) and evaluate_qa (160-163) have no status checks, so their failures fall through and run_cell ends with `echo "-> $cell done"` (returns 0). One overstatement: the `||` handler at 172-175 is not fully dead code — the smoke gate's explicit `return 2` (line 136) and the resume `return 0` (line 127) do exist, and a smoke failure reaches the handler. It is dead only for eval/scoring failures, which is the substantive claim. The resume-check consequence at line 124 holds as described.
findings.title: `run_cell ... || {...}` suspends set -e inside run_cell; gbrain eval and scoring failures are silently ignored and a partial run can be scored and locked in
findings.evidence: Line 172: `run_cell "$cell" ... || { rc=$?; ... }`. Per bash semantics, `set -e` is disabled for the entire body of a function invoked on the left of `||`. Verified in this sandbox: with `set -euo pipefail`, a `false` inside such a function falls through to the next statement. Consequences: (a) a failed `gbrain eval longmemeval` (line 152) falls through to the scoring step (line 161) which can score a PARTIAL/empty hypothesis file; (b) run_cell's last command is `echo "  -> $cell done: $scored"` so it returns 0 and the `||` handler at 172-175 is dead code; (c) if evaluate_qa produces `$scored` from a partial file, the resume check `[ -f "$scored" ]` (line 124) marks the cell permanently complete with a deflated accuracy number.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit checks inside run_cell: `if ! GBRAIN_... gbrain eval ...; then echo FAIL; return 3; fi` and `if ! (cd "$LONGMEMEVAL_REPO" && ...); then return 4; fi`, and only write a `.done` marker (or the scored file) after both succeed. Do not rely on set -e inside a function guarded by `||`.
findings.status_note: explicit step error handling + failure tally

findings.verifier_note: Lines 76-82 match exactly: `*0.35.1.0*|*0.35.2*|*0.36.*)` accepted, everything else exits 1 with a message that says 'need v0.35.1.0+'. Verified /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/package.json version is 0.47.6.0, which matches none of the patterns, and gbrain-evals package.json pins github:garrytan/gbrain#master. On a current install the script aborts before any cell.
findings.title: gbrain version gate is an allowlist of 0.35.x-0.36.x that rejects every newer version, including the repo's pinned gbrain (0.47.6.0)
findings.evidence: Lines 76-82: `case "$GBRAIN_VERSION" in *0.35.1.0*|*0.35.2*|*0.36.*) ;; *) echo "...need v0.35.1.0+ for --resume-from" >&2; exit 1;; esac`. The message says 'need v0.35.1.0+' but the pattern only accepts 0.35.1.0/0.35.2/0.36.x. The local gbrain checkout and the package.json dependency (`github:garrytan/gbrain#master`) are at version 0.47.6.0, so the script aborts before running any cell on a current install.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the allowlist with a minimum-version comparison (parse major/minor and test `>= 0.35.1`), e.g. `ver=$(gbrain --version | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'); if [ "$(printf '%s\n' 0.35 "$ver" | sort -V | head -1)" != 0.35 ]; then ... fi`.
findings.status_note: sort -V minimum gate

findings.verifier_note: grep of /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src for all three names returns zero hits. loadConfig's env fold (gbrain src/core/config.ts:712-713) reads only GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL/GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS (plus expansion/chat/multimodal keys); no reranker or search-mode env entries. Search mode is covered by the `--mode tokenmax` flag at line 154, but nothing enables the reranker, so even with the prefix bug fixed the A1/B1/C1/C2 receipts would measure the no-rerank pipeline. The file-plane key 'search.reranker.enabled' does exist (config.ts:1220), supporting the suggested fix channel.
findings.title: GBRAIN_RERANKER_MODEL / GBRAIN_SEARCH_RERANKER_ENABLED (and GBRAIN_SEARCH_MODE) env vars are not read anywhere in gbrain; reranker cells would run without reranking even if the prefix bug were fixed
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'GBRAIN_RERANKER_MODEL\|GBRAIN_SEARCH_RERANKER_ENABLED\|GBRAIN_SEARCH_MODE' /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src --include=*.ts` returns nothing in gbrain v0.47.6.0. loadConfig's env fold (gbrain src/core/config.ts:712-713) reads GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL and GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS but has no reranker or search-mode entries. Search mode is redundantly covered by the `--mode tokenmax` CLI flag (line 154), but nothing enables the reranker, so A1/B1/C1/C2 receipts would be labeled 'with zerank-2' while measuring the no-rerank pipeline: the with/without-reranker comparison would show a fake 0-point delta.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure the reranker through a channel gbrain actually reads: the file plane (~/.gbrain/config.json reranker_model + search.reranker.enabled via `gbrain config set`) or add a `--reranker` flag to `gbrain eval longmemeval`. Add a pre-flight assertion that the effective engine config shows reranker enabled before spending the cell budget.
findings.status_note: dead env vars removed; reranker cells refuse loudly

findings.verifier_note: Fetched the published xiaowu0162/LongMemEval src/evaluation/evaluate_qa.py: usage is `python evaluate_qa.py metric_model hyp_file ref_file` (3 positionals, no flags) and it writes to `hyp_file + '.eval-results-<model>'`. Correction to the failure mechanics: with the 4 flag args, len(sys.argv)=5 != 4, so the script prints usage and calls bare `exit()` — exit code 0 — meaning the miscall 'succeeds' without even needing the errexit-suspension to be swallowed. Either way $scored is never created, the resume check at line 124 never fires, and the phase prints '-> done' per cell with zero scored cells.
findings.title: evaluate_qa.py invoked with --input/--output flags and no reference file, which does not match LongMemEval's published evaluator interface
findings.evidence: Lines 160-163: `.venv/bin/python src/evaluation/evaluate_qa.py --input "$out" --output "$scored"`. The published LongMemEval evaluator (xiaowu0162/LongMemEval, referenced at line 27) takes positional arguments `<metric_model> <hypothesis_file> <reference_file>` and writes results to a derived `<hyp>.eval-results-<model>` path; it has no --input/--output flags, and no gold reference dataset is passed here at all. If the call fails, the errexit-suspension bug swallows it and `$scored` is never created, so the 'already scored' resume check at line 124 never fires and the phase ends with zero scored cells while printing '-> done' for each.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the published CLI: `(cd "$LONGMEMEVAL_REPO" && .venv/bin/python src/evaluation/evaluate_qa.py gpt-4o "$out" "$LONGMEMEVAL_DATASET")`, then copy/rename the evaluator's derived output file to "$scored"; fail the cell if the expected results file does not appear.
findings.status_note: published positional evaluate_qa interface

findings.verifier_note: Verified: run_cell (66-97) is invoked at line 101 with `|| { rc=$?; ... }`, which disables set -e (line 17) for the whole body (reproduced experimentally in bash 5.2.15). Both `bun run "$DRIVER"` calls (77 and 87) have no status check; unlike phase1, this run_cell has NO explicit return statements, so the last command `echo "-> $cell done"` (line 96) always returns 0 and the handler at 101-104 is truly dead. A failed cell prints '-> done' and the script ends with '[phase2] complete' and exit 0.
findings.title: Driver failures are silently swallowed: errexit is suspended inside run_cell and the || handler is dead code, so a failed cell prints '-> done'
findings.evidence: Line 101 invokes `run_cell ... || { rc=$?; ... }`, which disables `set -e` (line 17) for the whole function body (verified experimentally in bash). Inside run_cell, `bun run "$DRIVER" ...` (lines 77 and 87) has no explicit status check; on failure execution falls through, and run_cell's last command `echo "  -> $cell done"` (line 96) returns 0, so the handler at 101-104 can never fire. A cell whose embedder config is broken produces no receipt JSON yet the console and exit code report full success ('[phase2] complete').
findings.suggested_fix: Check each driver invocation explicitly: `if ! bun run "$DRIVER" ... ; then echo "  -> $cell FAILED (relational)" >&2; return 3; fi`, and at the end of the loop track a failure count and `exit 1` if any cell failed.
findings.status_note: phase2 step guards + non-zero on partial matrix

findings.verifier_note: smoke.ts:100 builds ~175K chars, line 104 calls `await embed([bigText])` (imported from 'gbrain/ai/gateway', which gbrain package.json exports maps to src/core/ai/gateway.ts). gateway.ts:104 `const MAX_CHARS = 8000`; the exported embed() (gateway.ts:1869) applies `texts.map(t => truncateUtf8(t ?? '', MAX_CHARS))` at line 1880, and truncateUtf8 (src/core/text-safe.ts:61) slices to maxChars. Providers only ever see ~8,000 chars (~2K tokens, below e.g. OpenAI's 8192-token embedding cap), so the phase cannot catch token-limit failures and the 'provider handled long input' log at line 109 is untrue.
findings.title: Phase 2 'long-haystack' gate is fake: gbrain's embed() truncates every input to 8,000 chars before the provider call, so the ~50K-token payload never reaches the API
findings.evidence: smoke.ts builds a 175K-char string (line 100) and claims to assert 'the embed call doesn't hit a token-limit error' (lines 14-16) via `await embed([bigText])` (line 104). But gbrain/src/core/ai/gateway.ts:104 defines `const MAX_CHARS = 8000` and gateway.ts:1880 applies `texts.map(t => truncateUtf8(t ?? '', MAX_CHARS))` inside embed() before any provider request. The provider only ever sees ~8,000 chars (~2K tokens), far below every provider's cap, so this phase can never catch the failure mode it exists to gate, and the success log 'provider handled long input' (line 109) is untrue.
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete Phase 2 (it duplicates Phase 1 wiring) or make it test what it claims: assert the gateway-level truncation policy explicitly (embed 175K chars and assert success BECAUSE truncation is expected, documenting that), or exercise the real long-content path the eval uses (e.g. importFromContent chunking on a 50K-token page) instead of a single embed() call.
findings.status_note: batch-volume long-haystack with distinct-vector assertion

findings.verifier_note: Line 297 prints the N header; lines 363/366 print the N=1 smoke and N=10 '~$200 Opus' repro tiers; package.json:24 ships eval:brainbench:published with BRAINBENCH_N=10. Repo-wide grep confirms BRAINBENCH_N is read only in all.ts:297 and multi-adapter.ts:285; multi-adapter.ts is not in CATEGORIES (lines 53-135) and none of the 10 subprocess scripts reference or import it. The dispatched run behaves identically at N=1 and N=10 while the report header asserts otherwise.
findings.title: Report header and repro instructions present BRAINBENCH_N as the run-count knob, but no dispatched subprocess Cat reads it
findings.evidence: Line 297 prints `**N:** ${process.env.BRAINBENCH_N ?? '5 (iteration default)'}` and lines 363-366 claim `BRAINBENCH_N=1` = smoke and `BRAINBENCH_N=10` = 'Published baseline (N=10, ~$200 Opus)'. A repo-wide grep shows BRAINBENCH_N is only read in all.ts and multi-adapter.ts, and multi-adapter.ts is NOT in CATEGORIES (lines 53-135) — none of the 10 subprocess scripts (before-after.ts, type-accuracy.ts, identity.ts, temporal.ts, cat6, perf, adversarial, cat11, mcp-contract, cat34) reference it. A 'published N=10' report is byte-identical in behavior to N=1 while its header asserts N=10, and package.json:24 ships the same fake knob as `eval:brainbench:published`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either thread BRAINBENCH_N into the Cat runners (loop N times and report mean±sd like multi-adapter.ts) or stop printing it: report per-Cat actual run counts, and drop the N=1/5/10 tiers from the repro block and package.json until they do something.
findings.status_note: BRAINBENCH_N doc honesty; CI uses per-job caps

findings.verifier_note: Line 348 calls precisionAtK(results, relevant, TOP_K); types.ts:258-264 returns `hits / topDocs.length` where topDocs = docs.slice(0, k), so 1 returned + 1 correct = 1.0 while 5 returned + 1 correct = 0.2. GbrainAfterAdapter's 'out' direction (Who attended X) returns graph hits only — the no-grep-fallback comment is at multi-adapter.ts:203 (finding said 199-203, close enough) — producing short lists, while HybridNoGraphAdapter returns long lists scored /5. before-after.ts:353-355 (min(TOP_K, returned) denominators) and shootout-driver.ts:199 share the convention as claimed.
findings.title: P@5 denominator is the returned-list length, not K, inflating adapters that return fewer than 5 results in the cross-adapter headline table
findings.evidence: Line 348 `totalP += precisionAtK(results, relevant, TOP_K)` uses types.ts:258-264, which returns `hits / topDocs.length` where `topDocs = docs.slice(0, k)` — an adapter returning 1 correct doc scores P@5 = 1.0 while an adapter returning 5 docs with 1 correct scores 0.2. This directly skews the neutral side-by-side: GbrainAfterAdapter's 'out'-direction path returns graph hits only with no fallback (lines 199-203, 'No explicit grep fallback for outgoing') and so routinely returns short lists, while HybridNoGraphAdapter always returns up to 20 docs and is always scored /5. before-after.ts:354-355 (`Math.min(TOP_K, r.beforeReturned)` denominators) and shootout-driver.ts:199 share the convention.

findings.verifier_note: Lines 174-190 verified: on timeout, child.kill('SIGTERM') at line 177 and the promise resolves immediately as fail (exit 124); no SIGKILL escalation exists anywhere. The worker loop (244-249) then starts the next Cat while a SIGTERM-ignoring child keeps running, defeating the concurrency=2 / ~800MB rationale documented at lines 9-11. The stdout/stderr listeners are never removed and keep appending to `output` after resolution (harmless to the already-resolved value, but accurate as stated).
findings.title: Timeout path sends SIGTERM only with no SIGKILL escalation; a hung cat keeps its ~400MB PGLite instance alive while the next cat starts
findings.evidence: Lines 174-190: on timeout the code does `child.kill('SIGTERM')` and immediately resolves the CategoryRun as failed; the worker loop then starts the next Cat. A child that ignores or slowly handles SIGTERM (the exact hang scenario the timeout exists for) keeps running and holding memory, defeating the 'caps peak memory around 800MB' concurrency rationale (lines 9-11), and its stdout listeners keep appending to `output` after the result was already resolved.
findings.suggested_fix: After SIGTERM, schedule `setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGKILL'), 10_000)` (cleared on 'close'), and detach/ignore further stdout data once settled.
findings.status_note: SIGKILL escalation

findings.evidence: main() (lines 188-429) computes beforePrecAtK/afterPrecAtK etc. but never compares them to any floor or to each other for exit-code purposes; the only non-zero exit is the crash handler at line 431. all.ts marks a Cat 'pass' purely on `exitCode === 0` (line 208), so a total retrieval regression (AFTER worse than BEFORE) would still show '✓ pass' in the published BrainBench summary table.
findings.suggested_fix: Exit non-zero when regression gates fail, e.g. `if (afterRecAtK < beforeRecAtK || afterPrecAtK < beforePrecAtK || afterRecAtK < 0.9) process.exit(1)` with the thresholds documented, so the BrainBench scorecard's pass column encodes quality, not just liveness. Also include the top-K headline metrics in the --json payload (currently only set-based before/after are emitted at lines 420-427).

units.unit_summary: Audited the LongMemEval unit (runner, aggregate, cache, chart, batch script, cache README) against gbrain v0.47.6 source and the official LongMemEval evaluator (xiaowu0162/LongMemEval on GitHub). All gbrain subpath imports exist except the fragile deep node_modules paths. Headline finding: the flagship number is computed as any-hit recall over all 500 questions, while the official benchmark metric is recall_all@k with the 30 abstention (_abs) questions excluded — the published head-to-head table therefore compares a looser metric on a different denominator against paper baselines (LongMemEval print_retrieval_metrics.py: `recall_all = float(all(...))`, `in_data = [x for x in in_data if '_abs' not in x['question_id']]`). Other confirmed bugs: NDJSON error rows permanently scored as misses on resume (aggregate also first-wins-dedupes successes away); aggregate hardcodes topK=5/dataset 's' while the runner defaults to k=8, mislabeling charts and baseline comparisons; embed-cache key fallback (text-embedding-3-large@1536) diverges from gbrain's actual gateway fallback (zembed-1@1280) and ignores query/document input_type for asymmetric models; empty-shard resume runs produce NaN metrics and crash fmt(); deep import of gbrain's nested ai-sdk breaks fresh non-linked installs; chart title hardcodes 'full 500 questions'; batch wrapper silently ignores user --dataset and hardcodes the 500-question completion target; warm-cache fixture docs (report says committed at eval/data/...) contradict the README (not committed) and the runner's default cacheDir (eval/reports/...). Improvements proposed: pin/record resolved gbrain search config (reranker/mode/model) in the report JSON, and seed the stratified sampler. Sources: github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval (src/evaluation/print_retrieval_metrics.py, src/retrieval/eval_utils.py, README.md), arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10813.

findings.verifier_note: Line 473 is exactly `const hit = retrieved.some(s => gt.has(s.toLowerCase()));` (any-hit). Fetched the official repo: src/retrieval/eval_utils.py computes `recall_all = float(all(doc in recalled_docs for doc in correct_docs))` and the print script (at src/evaluation/print_retrieval_metrics.py, not src/retrieval/) reports session-level metrics `['recall_all@5', 'ndcg_any@5', ...]` as headline. The report's section 5 table (docs/benchmarks/2026-05-07-longmemeval-s.md:113-124) puts the any-hit number in the same R@5 column as the paper's BM25/Stella/Contriever baselines, and section 6 shows multi-session (n=133, multi-evidence by construction) at 100.0%. Any-hit >= recall_all strictly for multi-evidence questions, so the inflation is mathematically real. The any-hit definition IS documented (runner header lines 5-8, report section 3), but that does not make the head-to-head comparison against recall_all-style published numbers valid.
findings.title: Recall@k is any-hit, not LongMemEval's official recall_all@k
findings.evidence: Line 473: `const hit = retrieved.some(s => gt.has(s.toLowerCase()));` — a question counts as recalled if ANY ground-truth session is in top-k. The official LongMemEval evaluator (src/retrieval/eval_utils.py) computes `recall_all = float(all(doc in recalled_docs for doc in correct_docs))` and its print_retrieval_metrics.py reports session-level `recall_all@5` as the headline. Multi-session questions (133/500) and many temporal-reasoning questions have multiple answer_session_ids, so any-hit strictly inflates the number vs the official metric. The published report (docs/benchmarks/2026-05-07-longmemeval-s.md, section 5) puts this any-hit number in a head-to-head table against 'BM25 (~70%) published baseline in the LongMemEval paper', Stella, and Contriever — all recall_all-style paper numbers — and shows multi-session at 100.0%, which is exactly the type any-hit inflates most.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute both recall_any@k and recall_all@k per question (hit_all = every gt session in retrieved top-k) and make recall_all@k the headline/comparison metric; keep any-hit only as a clearly-labeled secondary column. Also add ndcg_any@k to match the official script's output.
findings.status_note: Headline metric is now recall_all@k (official LongMemEval definition) computed via metrics.ts recallAllAtK on lowercased session ids; any-hit demoted to secondary field recall_any_at_k; ndcg_any_at_k added (metrics.ts ndcgAtK, binary grades). findings.verifier_note: Lines 286-289 load the dataset with no filter; grep for '_abs' across eval/runner/longmemeval*.ts returns nothing. Fetched the official repo: print_retrieval_metrics.py line `in_data = [x for x in in_data if '_abs' not in x['question_id']]` and README line 206 'for evaluating the retrieval, we always skip the 30 abstention instances... do not have a ground truth answer location' are verbatim as claimed. The published per-type table sums to n=500, confirming _abs questions were scored, vs the official 470-question protocol.
findings.title: Abstention (_abs) questions not excluded from retrieval recall
findings.evidence: Line 286-289 loads all questions with no filter: `const raw: Question[] = JSON.parse(readFileSync(opts.datasetPath, 'utf8')); let all = raw;` — no `_abs` handling anywhere in the file (grep for '_abs' in eval/runner/longmemeval.ts returns nothing). The official evaluator drops them first: `in_data = [x for x in in_data if '_abs' not in x['question_id']]` (print_retrieval_metrics.py), and the LongMemEval README states 'for evaluating the retrieval, we always skip the 30 abstention instances... these instances generally refer to non-existing events and do not have a ground truth answer location.' The runner scores 500 questions where the official protocol scores 470, making the denominator (and every per-type recall containing _abs variants) non-comparable to published numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter `all = all.filter(q => !q.question_id.endsWith('_abs'))` before scoring (or bucket _abs separately and exclude from recall_at_k and recall_by_type), matching the official protocol; note the exclusion in the report JSON.
findings.status_note: _abs questions (question_id.includes('_abs'), the official substring rule) are excluded from every recall denominator (overall and per-type) and reported separately as abs_noise@k = fraction of top-k slots holding claimed-evidence sessions (metrics.ts precisionAtK). Exclusion is stamped in the repor

findings.verifier_note: errRow (lines 507-516) includes adapter+question_id and error:msg, appended at 518-519. readCompletedPairs (124-138) marks a pair done on `obj?.adapter && obj?.question_id` alone, never checking obj.error, so the resume skip at line 418 permanently drops errored questions (90s timeout at line 394, API errors) as hit_at_k:false misses. Design comment at 367-368 ('at worst we lose the current question and resume on the next') is contradicted for caught errors. Aggregate dedupe is first-wins (longmemeval-aggregate.ts:48-57), so a later success row from a racing worker is the one dropped. Minor mitigation: the aggregate's markdown shows an Errors column, but recall_at_k still counts error rows as misses.
findings.title: Error rows written to NDJSON become permanent misses on resume
findings.evidence: Lines 507-519: the catch block builds `errRow = { ...hit_at_k: false, ...error: msg }` and appends it: `appendFileSync(opts.ndjsonPath, JSON.stringify({ adapter: adapter.name, ...errRow }) + '\n');`. `readCompletedPairs` (lines 124-138) marks a pair done whenever `obj?.adapter && obj?.question_id` exist — it never checks `error`. So a transient failure (the 90s WASM-abort timeout this very file documents at line 388-394, an OpenAI 429, etc.) is recorded as a miss and skipped forever by every restarted batch, silently deflating recall. This contradicts the design comment at line 367-368: 'at worst we lose the current question and resume on the next.' Compounding it, longmemeval-aggregate.ts lines 49-56 dedupe first-wins, so if a racing worker later succeeds on the same pair, the success row is the one dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: In readCompletedPairs, skip rows where `obj.error` is set so errored questions are retried on the next batch (MAX_BATCHES=50 already bounds pathological retry loops); in the aggregate, prefer a non-error row over an error row when deduping duplicates.
findings.status_note: readCompletedPairs now skips rows carrying an error field, so errored questions re-run on the next invocation (MAX_BATCHES bounds retries); truncated final NDJSON lines are tolerated and re-run. longmemeval-aggregate.ts dedupeRows prefers the non-error row when a success and an error row share a key

findings.verifier_note: Line 93 `topK: 5, // assumed; the NDJSON doesn't carry topK`, line 111 writes opts {datasetName:'s', topK:5}, line 120 prints 'Top-K: 5'. NDJSON rows carry neither topK nor dataset (runner line 486 spreads only the row fields). Runner default is k=8 (longmemeval.ts:101) and batch.sh's header documents a `--top-k 8` invocation (line 26; its own default TOP_K=5 at line 39). Chart trusts opts.topK: title `recall@${topK}` (line 159 and 247) and R@5 baseline inclusion via `EXTERNAL_BASELINES.filter(b => b.topK === topK)` (line 110), so a k=8 or oracle NDJSON aggregates into a mislabeled recall@5 chart with R@5 baselines. The 'assumed' comment documents the assumption but does not prevent the mislabeling.
findings.title: Aggregate hardcodes topK=5 and dataset 's'; mislabels k=8 runs
findings.evidence: Line 93: `topK: 5, // assumed; the NDJSON doesn't carry topK` and line 111 writes `opts: { datasetName: 's', topK: 5 }`; line 120 prints `Top-K: 5`. But the runner's actual default is 8 (longmemeval.ts:101 `topK: Number(arg(args, '--top-k') ?? '8')`), and longmemeval-batch.sh's header documents `--top-k 8` runs. Any NDJSON produced at k!=5 gets published as 'Recall@5', and longmemeval-chart.ts then trusts `opts.topK` to (a) title the chart `recall@${topK}` and (b) include R@5 external baselines via `EXTERNAL_BASELINES.filter(b => b.topK === topK)` (chart line 110) — i.e. an R@8 run gets charted head-to-head against MemPal's R@5 numbers with a 'recall@5' label. `dataset: 's'` is likewise wrong for oracle NDJSONs.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the runner include `topK` and `dataset` in every NDJSON row (it already spreads the row object at longmemeval.ts:486); in the aggregate, read them from the rows, error on mixed values, and stop hardcoding 5/'s'. As a stopgap, accept `--top-k`/`--dataset` CLI args.
findings.status_note: Runner stamps top_k and dataset into every NDJSON row; aggregate reads them via inferRunParams — mixed values are a hard error, legacy streams without the fields require explicit --top-k/--dataset (never a hardcoded 5/'s'), and a CLI flag contradicting the rows is an error. Chart titles use the inpu

findings.verifier_note: Lines 347-348 fall back to 'text-embedding-3-large'/1536. Verified in the local gbrain checkout (v0.47.6.0): gateway.ts:465 `embedding_model: config.embedding_model ?? DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` with defaults.ts:26-27 = 'zeroentropyai:zembed-1' @ 1280 (legacy configless fallback; new-install default is voyage-4@1024, defaults.ts:47-48). So a configless machine caches real zembed-1@1280 vectors under key 'text-embedding-3-large@1536', falsifying the auto-invalidation guarantee in the comment at 342-346 and embed-cache/README.md. Poisoning consequence verified: the gateway's post-transport dim check throws 'Embedding dim mismatch' (gateway.ts:2148-2153) per batch, which the per-question catch (lines 496-521) converts to hit_at_k:false rows. getEmbeddingModel/getEmbeddingDimensions getters exist in the gateway for the suggested fix.
findings.title: Cache-key fallback model/dims differ from gateway's actual fallback
findings.evidence: Lines 347-348: `const cacheModel = cfg.embedding_model || 'text-embedding-3-large'; const cacheDims = cfg.embedding_dimensions || 1536;`. But configureGateway applies `config.embedding_model ?? DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` (gbrain gateway.ts:465) where DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL = 'zeroentropyai:zembed-1' and DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS = 1280 (gbrain src/core/ai/defaults.ts:26-27, v0.47.6). On a machine with no embedding_model in config, real zembed-1@1280 vectors are cached under the key 'text-embedding-3-large@1536' — the 'content-addressed, auto-invalidating' guarantee in the comment at lines 342-346 and in embed-cache/README.md is false. Sharing that cache file (which the README explicitly encourages) then poisons a genuinely-3-large@1536 machine: the gateway's dim check throws 'Embedding dim mismatch' per batch, which the per-question catch converts into hit_at_k:false rows — silent score deflation.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the cache key from the gateway's resolved values after configureGateway — `getEmbeddingModel()` and `getEmbeddingDimensions()` are exported from gbrain/ai/gateway — instead of re-deriving with fallbacks that can drift from gbrain's defaults.
findings.status_note: Cache model/dims now read from the gateway's RESOLVED values (getEmbeddingModel()/getEmbeddingDimensions() after configureGateway) instead of a local 'text-embedding-3-large'/1536 fallback that had drifted from gbrain's actual configless fallback (zembed-1@1280). units.unit_summary: Audited the agentic-cats unit (cat5/cat8/cat9 runners, tool-bridge, recorder, mcp-contract) against gbrain v0.47.6 source and the published eval schemas. The judge-blinding core holds: cat9's buildEvidence sends only the structured digest (no raw tool_result content), and the bridge's poison tagging + expand-stripping match the gbrain operations registry (all 12 exposed ops exist and are non-mutating; `query.expand` is both schema-stripped and executor-forced false, with the only hidden-LLM escape hatch — CRAG escalation — config-gated off by default). Found 16 bugs and 3 improvements. Most severe: any OperationError from a gbrain handler (routine agent misbehavior like a malformed slug) rethrows out of the agent loop and destroys the entire Cat 8/9 run; cat5's prompt literally tells the classifier '(...almost certainly unsupported)' for every gold-unsupported claim, inflating citation_accuracy; judge.ts's weightedMean computes the mean over the judge's returned scores rather than the rubric, so omitted criteria silently inflate overall_score; mcp-contract's traverse_graph depth-cap assertion cannot fail and its claimed trusted-vs-remote matrix never tests remote=false; brain_first_ordering mislabels no-answer runs as 'answer_before_brain'; 'rate_limit_exhausted' is dead code; and turn-capped empty answers pass citation_format/back_link vacuously. Contract drift: emitted transcripts/evidence violate the published schemas (probe_id pattern, probe.text vs query) and OperationContext literals omit the TS-required sourceId. The flight-recorder is entirely unwired (emitBundle has no runner callers).

findings.title: Any gbrain OperationError from a tool call crashes the entire Cat 8/9 run
findings.evidence: In the tool-execution loop only bridge errors are converted to tool_result blocks: `if (err instanceof ForbiddenOpError || err instanceof UnknownToolError) { toolResult = {...} } else { throw err; }` (lines 303-311). tool-bridge.ts:415 calls `await op.handler(ctx, safeInput)` with no try/catch, so every gbrain OperationError propagates here. gbrain handlers throw on completely normal agent misbehavior: `validatePageSlug` (gbrain src/core/ops/context.ts) throws `OperationError('invalid_params', ...)` for a slug with a space or '@', `resolveRequestedScope` throws `permission_denied`, `add_timeline_entry`-style validation throws plain Error. The rethrow rejects `runAgentLoop`, which rejects the worker promise inside `runConcurrently` (cat8-skill-compliance.ts:190-209 / cat9-workflows.ts:112-131), and `Promise.all` rejects — the whole 50-scenario run dies and every completed probe result is discarded.

Alternatively catch per-probe in runCat8/runCat9 and record a `probe_errored` outcome instead of losing the run.

findings.verifier_note: Exact at line 163: '(no source pages provided — the claim is almost certainly unsupported)' whenever sources.length === 0. Sources are resolved solely from gold claim.expected_evidence (runCat5 lines 367-373), documented as 'Slugs of pages that should support the claim when expected_label=supported' — so gold-unsupported claims get zero sources and the judge is handed the answer; the class is also separable by source count alone. Caveat: eval/data/gold/citations.json currently ships as a template with a single supported example, so no unsupported claims exist yet; the leak fires on any gold set authored to the documented field semantics. The same hint also fires (wrongly) for supported claims whose evidence slugs fail to resolve (see the cat5:371 silent-drop finding).
findings.title: Prompt leaks the gold label to the classifier for every 'unsupported' claim
findings.evidence: `renderClaimPrompt` pushes `'  (no source pages provided — the claim is almost certainly unsupported)'` when `sources.length === 0`. Sources are resolved from the GOLD field `claim.expected_evidence` (runCat5, lines 368-373), which is empty exactly when `expected_label === 'unsupported'`. So for every gold-unsupported claim the judge is literally told the expected answer, and the 'unsupported' class is also trivially separable by source count alone. `citation_accuracy` (the headline metric, threshold >0.90 per the module doc) is inflated for that entire class — the eval measures nothing about unsupported-claim detection.

Better: give the classifier a fixed evidence context independent of the gold label — e.g. the claim's `source_page` content plus retrieved candidate pages including distractors — so class membership is not encoded in the input shape.

findings.verifier_note: Exact. weightedMean (lines 241-252) iterates the judge's scores array; line 247 gives unknown criterion_ids weight 1 via `?? 1`; duplicates are double-counted; omitted rubric criteria simply vanish from the mean. parseToolUse (lines 268-299) validates shape only, never rubric coverage. scoreAnswer line 389/393 derives the verdict from this mean, and cat9-workflows.ts:199 sets pass from that verdict. A 2-of-4-criteria response scoring 5 yields overall 5.0 = pass.
findings.title: weightedMean silently drops rubric criteria the judge omitted and counts unknown/duplicate criterion ids
findings.evidence: `weightedMean(scores, rubric)` iterates over the JUDGE'S returned `scores` array, not the rubric: `for (const s of scores) { const w = weightById.get(s.criterion_id) ?? 1; totalScore += s.score * w; totalWeight += w; }` (lines 246-250). `parseToolUse` never checks that every rubric criterion is present. If Haiku returns 2 of 4 criteria with score 5, overall_score = 5.0 and the computed verdict is 'pass' even though half the rubric was never graded. Conversely a hallucinated criterion_id not in the rubric gets weight 1 (`?? 1`) and enters the mean, and a duplicated criterion is double-counted. Cat 9 pass/fail (cat9-workflows.ts:199 `pass: judgeResult.verdict === 'pass'`) rides directly on this number.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the mean over the RUBRIC: for each rubric criterion take the judge's matching score (treat missing as 0, or trigger the retry path like a malformed response), ignore scores whose criterion_id is not in the rubric, and dedupe by criterion_id.

findings.verifier_note: Exact. computeBrainFirstOrdering (lines 402-418): line 412 returns no_brain_calls when zero brain reads, line 416 returns brain_before_answer when an answer exists, so line 417's 'answer_before_brain' fires only for brainCalls>0 with no final answer (turn-cap runs). findings.title: brain_first_ordering reports 'answer_before_brain' for runs that produced NO answer; the intended case is unreachable
findings.evidence: `computeBrainFirstOrdering` returns `'answer_before_brain'` only when `brainCalls.length > 0 && !finalAnswerProduced` — i.e. turn-cap or loop-abort runs where no final answer exists at all. Meanwhile a genuine answer-before-brain ordering is structurally impossible in this harness: the loop only records a final answer when a response has no tool_use blocks (line 273), so any recorded answer necessarily follows every tool call, making `brain_before_answer` automatic whenever >=1 brain call happened. The mislabel flows into Cat 8 per-probe reports (`brain_first` field) and into the judge via `tool_call_summary.brain_first_ordering` (cat9-workflows.ts:160), telling the judge the agent 'answered before consulting the brain' when it never answered.
