findings.verifier_note: Exact. Retry loop lines 208-234: attempt increments only inside `isRateLimitError(err) && attempt < maxRetries - 1`, so attempt maxes at maxRetries-1 and the while condition never goes false; the loop exits only via break (response set) or `throw err` at line 232 — which fires for a rate-limit error on the final attempt. The `if (!response)` branch at 235-239 is dead for any maxRetries >= 1 (default 3). A sustained 429 therefore rejects runAgentLoop and, via runConcurrently/Promise.all in runCat8/runCat9, destroys the whole run instead of recording the documented graceful stop_reason.
findings.title: stop_reason 'rate_limit_exhausted' is unreachable — exhausted retries throw and kill the whole run
findings.evidence: The retry loop's failure arm is `if (isRateLimitError(err) && attempt < maxRetries - 1) { await sleep(...); attempt++; continue; } throw err;` (lines 226-232). On the final attempt (attempt === maxRetries-1) a rate-limit error hits `throw err`, so the loop can only exit via `break` (response set) or throw. The graceful path `if (!response) { stopReason = 'rate_limit_exhausted'; ... break; }` (lines 235-239) is dead code. A sustained 429 therefore rejects runAgentLoop and (via Promise.all in runCat8/runCat9) destroys the whole run instead of recording the documented 'rate_limit_exhausted' result.
findings.suggested_fix: On the last attempt, `break` out of the retry loop with response still null (for rate-limit errors) so the existing `if (!response)` branch records stop_reason='rate_limit_exhausted' and the probe completes with partial data.
findings.status_note: Duplicate of adapters-queries-01; same retry-loop fix. runCat8/runCat9 additionally convert stop_reason==='rate_limit_exhausted' results into acc.error(id,'dependency',...) so throttled probes are excluded + capped, never scored.

findings.verifier_note: Exact (has-check at line 236, add at 237). The WeakSet accumulates every visited object and is never pruned, so JSON.stringify's per-occurrence replacer turns the second and later occurrences of any shared (non-cyclic) reference into the string '[Circular]' — the classic seen-set-vs-ancestor-path bug. Consequence is real for any scorecard/brain-export containing a reused object (e.g. a rubric array or config object referenced from multiple probes within one stringify call); each file gets its own fresh WeakSet, so corruption is per-artifact. Currently latent in practice since runners never call emitBundle (see the wiring finding), but the defect is exactly as described.
findings.title: safeStringify replaces shared (non-cyclic) object references with '[Circular]', corrupting bundle JSON
findings.evidence: The replacer uses a WeakSet that objects are added to but never removed from: `if (seen.has(v as object)) return '[Circular]'; seen.add(v as object);`. JSON.stringify legitimately visits a shared reference once per occurrence, so any object referenced twice in a scorecard/brain-export (e.g. one rubric array or config object reused across probes, a shared edges array) serializes as the string "[Circular]" on every occurrence after the first — silent data loss in scorecard.json / brain-export.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the current ancestor path instead of all-visited objects (delete from the set after serializing each subtree), or use a path-stack-based cycle detector so only true cycles are replaced.
findings.status_note: safeStringify now decycles with an ancestor-path Set (added on subtree entry, deleted on exit), so only true cycles become '[Circular]'; shared non-cyclic references serialize in full at every occurrence. toJSON (Date) honored, Float32/Float64Array still converted to plain arrays.

units.unit_summary: Audited the four retrieval-cat runners end to end, tracing every gbrain import into the local v0.47.6.0 checkout (export map, extractPageLinks/stripCodeBlocks, hybridSearch, importFromContent, gateway/embedding, source-boost SQL) and inspecting the committed corpora (world-v1: 240 pages, ~6 links/page; source-swamp-v1: all 30 query slugs verified present). Three critical findings: cat13 and cat13b's inline gbrain adapters never call configureGateway, which gbrain v0.40+ requires before any embed, so both runners crash in the first adapter's init (with console silenced) — the repo's own HybridNoGraphAdapter documents and fixes exactly this; and cat11 is unrunnable as shipped (no fixtures, and the documented `bun run eval:fetch-multimodal` script does not exist), yet exits 0 so all.ts records the category as PASS. Major metric-integrity findings: cat6's link_precision divides injected-gold matches by all extracted links including ~6 unlabeled legitimate base links per page (perfect extractor ≈ 0.22); cat6's prose_only_mention recall is structurally 0 and substring_fp_rate structurally 0 (gold requires bare-name linking no exercised code path performs); cat13b's swamp prefix wintermute/chat/ was renamed to openclaw/chat/ in gbrain v0.24.0 so the demotion half of the source-boost signal has been silently untested ever since (and the published report's 0.5x claim is stale); cat13b's 80% pass criterion never affects exit code or any artifact; cat13's semantic-neighborhood template emits identical query texts with conflicting golds; cat11's mean_metric drops failed items, its documented thresholds are never applied (verdict pass/fail unreachable), and its PDF/HTML rows benchmark eval-local extractors rather than gbrain. Engine hygiene checked out: PGLiteEngine.connect({}) is in-memory (database_path undefined), each adapter gets a fresh engine with teardown/disconnect, and sanitizePage/sanitizeQuery correctly strip _facts/gold before adapters see them. Three improvements proposed: a source-boost-off ablation for cat13b, seeded Fisher-Yates for cat13 probe sampling, and sha256 verification of cat11 fixtures.

findings.verifier_note: All load-bearing evidence verified in source: the inline adapter calls importFromContent (line 425) with no configureGateway; gbrain master is v0.47.6.0 and _config starts null (ai/gateway.ts:135); requireConfig throws at gateway.ts:813-818 (message at 815-816); importFromContent embeds by default (opts.noEmbed unset; import-file.ts:902-911 via embedBatchWithBackoff -> embedBatch -> gateway.embed -> requireConfig) and the propagation comment is at import-file.ts:845; nothing in PGLiteEngine.connect/importFromContent or any module-load side effect configures the gateway (all configureGateway calls live in cli.ts/command entrypoints; configureGatewayIfUninitialized is only called by enrich/extract-conversation-facts); HybridNoGraphAdapter documents and works around this at adapters/vector-grep-rrf-fusion.ts:69-77; gbrain is first in allAdapters (line 537). One sub-claim is wrong: the error is NOT invisible — the finally block (lines 429-432) restores console.log/error before the exception reaches main().catch (line 584), which prints it and exits 1. The crash is loud, but the core defect (default run dies before any adapter scores) is real. UNCERTAIN-adjacent caveat: not executed (node_modules absent), but every step of the failure chain is verified statically.
findings.title: GbrainAfterAdapter never configures the AI gateway; init crashes under gbrain v0.47
findings.evidence: GbrainAfterAdapter.init() calls `await importFromContent(engine, p.slug, fm.join('\n'))` (line 425) with no prior configureGateway call. In gbrain v0.47.6.0, import-file.ts:845 states 'embedding failure PROPAGATES' and embeds inline via embedBatchWithBackoff (import-file.ts:911); gateway.embed() calls requireConfig() which throws 'AI gateway is not configured. Call configureGateway() during engine connect.' (ai/gateway.ts:816) because `_config` starts null and nothing in PGLiteEngine.connect/importFromContent initializes it. The repo's own HybridNoGraphAdapter documents this: 'v0.40+ requires the gateway to be explicitly configured before any embed call' (adapters/vector-grep-rrf-fusion.ts:69-71) and calls configureGateway; the inline gbrain adapter was never updated. Since 'gbrain' is first in allAdapters (line 537), the default full run throws before any adapter scores, and errors during init are invisible because console.log/error are no-op'd (lines 407-409).
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror HybridNoGraphAdapter: at the top of init(), call configureGateway({ embedding_model: 'openai:text-embedding-3-large', embedding_dimensions: 1536, env: process.env }) (imported from 'gbrain/ai/gateway'), or drop the inline adapter and reuse HybridNoGraphAdapter's init plus runExtract.

findings.verifier_note: Verified structurally and empirically. Line 328's text depends only on the neighbor np, not the source concept; coOccur is symmetric; grades set c=3, neighbors (incl. np)=1 (lines 356-358); dedup is per-concept (seen created inside the concept loop, line 342). Replicating the generator against world-v1's 30 concept pages yields 31 duplicate probe texts emitted by different concepts with conflicting grade-3 targets — e.g. 'concepts related to fine-tuning' from 6 concepts, and company-seeded 'frameworks that come up when discussing apex-18' / 'lucid-labs-71' (lines 334-338), which also confirms the slug-tail leak. A deterministic retriever necessarily scores wrong on all but one twin, capping nDCG for the template. (The per-concept shuffle/slice can drop some twins in a given run but nothing dedupes across concepts.)
findings.title: semantic-neighborhood probes create identical query texts with conflicting golds
findings.evidence: For each concept c, line 328 generates `concepts related to ${np._facts.name...}` where np is a NEIGHBOR of c, with gold grade 3 on c and only grade 1 on np (lines 356-358). Co-occurrence is symmetric, so two concepts A and C that both neighbor B each emit the literal text 'concepts related to <B>' — one demanding A at rank 1, the other demanding C. Dedup is per-concept only (`seen` reset inside the loop, line 342), so both survive; a deterministic retriever returns one ranking for the same string and is scored wrong on the other, structurally capping nDCG for this template. The probe's most on-topic page (B itself) is graded 1, further penalizing correct behavior. Same defect for the company-seeded probes (lines 334-338), which also leak slug tails ('discussing acme-0') into query text.
findings.suggested_fix: Grade the named concept and its neighborhood relative to the query text (target = np's neighbor set, np graded too), dedupe probe texts globally across concepts, and use `title` instead of the slug tail for company-seeded probes.
findings.status_note: Semantic-neighborhood probes are now grounded in the query text: 'concepts related to <X>' is emitted exactly once, for concept X itself (gold X=3, X's co-occurrence neighbors=1), never once per neighbor with conflicting golds. findings.verifier_note: Verified: line 351 is [...unique].sort(() => rng() - 0.5).slice(0, perConcept) — a random comparator, whose output and number of comparator invocations depend on the engine's sort implementation, so the sampled probe set is stable only within one runtime version; the methodology at line 576 claims 'Rerun produces identical set' without that qualifier. Because a single shared mulberry32 stream (line 83) feeds all concepts, an implementation-defined number of draws in one concept's shuffle also perturbs every later concept's sample, exactly as claimed.
findings.title: Biased sort-comparator shuffle undermines the cross-runtime determinism claim
findings.evidence: `[...unique].sort(() => rng() - 0.5).slice(0, perConcept)` (line 351). A random comparator is a biased shuffle and its output depends on the engine's sort algorithm and comparator call order, so the methodology claim 'Rerun produces identical set' (line 576) only holds within one Bun version; a runtime upgrade silently changes which templates each concept's probes sample, breaking baseline comparability. It also consumes an implementation-defined number of rng() draws, perturbing every later concept's sample.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle (fixed rng draws per element) so probe selection is stable across runtimes and unbiased.
findings.status_note: Replaced [...unique].sort(() => rng() - 0.5) with an exported seededShuffle() (Fisher-Yates): unbiased, consumes exactly n-1 rng draws per call regardless of the JS engine's sort implementation, so the sampled probe set is stable across runtimes and one concept's shuffle can never perturb a later co

units.unit_summary: Audited the calibration-cats unit: eval/runner/cat14-calibration.ts (calibration A/B gate), its paired test file, and eval/runner/cat15-propose-takes.ts (extractor precision/recall gate), plus the cat14/cat15 fixture dirs and the gbrain v0.47.6.0 checkout they claim to mirror. Fixture integrity is good (8 cat14 probes with all 6 categories; all 8 cat15 page/ground-truth pairs exist in gbrain's test/fixtures/calibration with 4-10 claims each). The big problems are integrity-of-measurement, not arithmetic: cat14 never touches gbrain code despite header/README claims (hand-rolled prompts diverge sharply from gbrain's real JSON-structured think prompt, resolved_takes never seeded) — critical; cat15's mirrored extractor prompt has drifted from production (conviction vs weight, missing holder + dedup block) and its P/R/F1 are computed from unvalidated judge lists whose omissions silently inflate both metrics; cat14's implemented gates drop the README's two core positive-axis gates and the behaves_like_baseline check, its judge receives the probe notes that state the expected verdict, and the 55% win-rate denominator counts structurally-tie probes (empty-profile probe compares two samples of the identical prompt) and judge failures. cat15's default corpus dir is a machine-specific Conductor path that throws on the documented default invocation. Minor issues: both-empty F1=0 convention, a missing cat15 README the failure output points at, and a test header claiming a dry-run execution no test performs (file also sits outside the `bun test test/eval/` script glob). Top improvements: temperature control for an 8-probe gate, blinded/randomized A/B labels for the judge, and run provenance in _summary.json so dry-run/partial summaries can't masquerade as real passes.

findings.verifier_note: The runner imports only @anthropic-ai/sdk, fs, path, url — zero gbrain imports and no child_process shell-out. Header lines 10-16 claim PGLite seeding and gbrain's exported buildThinkSystemPrompt/buildThinkUserMessage/buildCalibrationBlock; the README (line 117) claims a 'Shell-out runner against gbrain think CLI'. Neither happens: buildBaselineSystemPrompt (line 126-128) is a one-liner advice-voice prompt, while gbrain's shipped THINK_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BASE (/home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src/core/think/prompt.ts lines 40-70) demands JSON-only output, <pages>/<takes>/<graph> evidence tags, citations, and 'Never instruct the user (no "you should" / "I recommend X")' — the opposite behavior. gbrain's buildCalibrationBlock renders <calibration> in the user message (prompt.ts lines 113-130, D22); the eval injects <calibration_profile> into the system prompt. brain_setup.resolved_takes appears only at the interface declaration (line 54); grep confirms it is never read by the runner. The consequence is real: the gate certifies a prompt gbrain does not ship.
findings.title: cat14 never exercises gbrain: hand-rolled prompt mirror replaces the shipped think pipeline
findings.evidence: Header (lines 10-16) claims 'Seed an in-memory PGLite brain' and 'Build baseline + calibrated system+user prompts via gbrain's exported buildThinkSystemPrompt / buildThinkUserMessage / buildCalibrationBlock helpers', and the README claims v1 ships a 'Shell-out runner against gbrain think CLI (tests the real user path end-to-end)'. The file imports nothing from gbrain; it defines local buildBaselineSystemPrompt() (line 126: 'You are gbrain's synthesis engine... Be direct... Conversational voice — friend, not doctor.') and buildCalibratedSystemPrompt(). gbrain's real prompt (/home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src/core/think/prompt.ts THINK_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BASE) is materially different: it wraps evidence in <pages>/<takes>/<graph>, demands 'Output MUST be valid JSON matching the schema below', and says 'Never instruct the user (no "you should" / "I recommend X")' — the opposite of the eval's advice-giving prompt. buildCalibrationBlock in gbrain renders a <calibration> block in the user message per D22; the eval injects a differently-shaped <calibration_profile> into the system prompt. Also brain_setup.resolved_takes (interface line 54) is never referenced anywhere in the runner — no brain is seeded. The A/B gate therefore certifies a prompt experiment that gbrain does not ship.
findings.suggested_fix: Import buildThinkSystemPrompt/buildThinkUserMessage/buildCalibrationBlock from the gbrain checkout (add a './think/prompt' subpath export or re-export from src/core/think/index.ts), build prompts with {withCalibration: true} + calibration opts from the probe profile, and render resolved_takes into the takesBlock so the model sees the same evidence surface production sees. At minimum, add a test asserting the mirrored prompt strings equal gbrain's exported ones so drift fails loudly.

findings.verifier_note: Lines 312-314 match the quoted code exactly. Recall's denominator is tp+fn = match.matches.length (judge-returned list), not groundTruth.length; the MATCH_TOOL schema description (line 201) asks for 'One entry per ground-truth claim' but nothing validates count, index range, or duplicates. A judge returning 4 matched entries against 6 GT claims yields recall 4/4=1.0. Extracted claims listed in neither matches nor false_positives inflate precision (fp = false_positives.length, line 314), duplicate extracted_index values double-count tp, and out-of-range indices are counted blind. Failure scenario is real.
findings.title: Precision/recall computed from unvalidated judge output; omissions silently inflate both
findings.evidence: Lines 312-314: `const tp = match ? match.matches.filter(m => m.extracted_index !== null).length : 0; const fn = match ? match.matches.filter(m => m.extracted_index === null).length : groundTruth.length; const fp = match ? match.false_positives.length : extracted.length;`. Recall's denominator is tp+fn = match.matches.length, the judge-returned list length, not groundTruth.length — if the Haiku judge returns fewer entries than ground-truth claims (nothing enforces one-per-GT), the missing claims vanish from the denominator and recall inflates (e.g. 6 GT claims, judge returns 4 matched entries -> recall 4/4 = 1.0). Symmetrically, extracted claims the judge lists in neither matches nor false_positives inflate precision, two GT entries pointing at the same extracted_index double-count tp, and out-of-range/duplicate indices in false_positives are counted blind.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the tool output: require exactly one match entry per ground-truth index (fill missing ones as FN, i.e. fn = groundTruth.length - uniqueMatchedGT), dedupe extracted_index values (second use of the same index is not a TP), clamp indices to range, and derive fp = extracted.length - uniqueMatchedExtracted instead of trusting false_positives.length. Retry the judge when validation fails.
findings.status_note: Judge match_claims output is now validated before any metric math: exactly one entry per ground-truth index (missing/duplicate rejected), extracted_index values unique and in range (no double-counted TPs), false_positives in range/deduped/disjoint, and every extracted claim accounted exactly once ac

findings.verifier_note: Line 389 is exact (winRate = winCal/total, total = all results); only win_overall==='calibrated' counts (line 364); ties and judge_failed (line 333 default) deflate the rate. For cat14-neg-1-empty-profile, buildCalibratedSystemPrompt lines 131-134 return the baseline prompt verbatim, so both answers are samples of an identical prompt — any 'calibrated' verdict is noise. Five of the 8 probes expect baseline-equivalent output (pos-2, pos-4, neg-1, neg-2, neg-4 all have changes_recommendation_meaningfully:false), so honest ties there cap win rate at 3/8=37.5%, under the 55% gate — the finding's <=4/8 bound is conservative but correct. The committed iteration log corroborates: v1 passed at 75% win only because the (unblinded) judge awarded 'calibrated' on tie-designed probes; v1 had 25% ties and barely cleared.
findings.title: Win-rate gate denominator counts probes whose only correct verdict is tie, plus judge failures
findings.evidence: Line 389: `const winRate = total > 0 ? winCal / total : 0;` with total = all probes and only win_overall === 'calibrated' counting as a win (line 364); ties and judge_failed count against the 55% gate. For cat14-neg-1-empty-profile, buildCalibratedSystemPrompt falls through to the baseline prompt verbatim (lines 131-134), so both answers are two samples from the identical prompt — an honest judge must say 'tie' (any 'calibrated' verdict is sampling noise), yet that tie lowers win rate. cat14-neg-2 and the three changes_recommendation_meaningfully:false probes similarly expect baseline-equivalent output ('Calibrated wins only if it adds genuine signal' per the tool description). With 8 probes, honest ties on those cases yield <= 4/8 = 50% and the gate fails on perfect behavior; a transient judge API failure (win_overall='judge_failed', line 333) has the same deflating effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute win rate over win-eligible probes only (exclude judge_failed, and exclude or score-as-correct the categories whose expected outcome is tie: empty-profile, bias-irrelevant), or gate on 'calibrated wins among non-tie verdicts' plus a separate tie-correctness check for negative probes. Fail loudly (nonzero exit) when judge_failed > 0 instead of folding it into win rate.

units.unit_summary: Audited cats 18-21 (5 runners) against gbrain v0.47.6.0 source. Three critical findings: (1) cat21 ingests only the first 60 of 857 files under src/core, excluding 11 of 12 gold-target files (verified by simulating the walk), so both embedder cells score ~0 and the eval measures nothing; (2) cat18/cat18b Recall@10 counts duplicate chunk rows per relevant page (gbrain dedup returns up to 2 chunks/page), inflating recall past 100%; (3) cat18's 'embedding provider A/B' silently runs gbrain's default balanced-mode zerank-2 reranker in every cell (mode.ts:400 reranker_enabled:true), so the headline comparison backing the 'ZE beats OpenAI/Voyage' README claim is embedder+ZE-reranker, contradicting cat18b's 'no-reranker baseline' framing; cat21 has the same env-dependent hidden-reranker contamination on its top-1 metric. Major integrity issues: cat18b's '±rerank' axis is confounded with a full balanced-to-tokenmax mode-bundle switch (expansion, token budget, relational recall all flip too); cat18b/cat21 swallow ingest/query errors with bare catch and both gbrain's reranker and vector arm are fail-open, so broken-key cells publish keyword-only/unreranked numbers under their intended labels with zero receipt evidence; cat19 reads BrainHealth fields that don't exist (chunk_count/link_count), so its before/after link metric always prints 0, and despite header claims ('assert it climbed', doctor recommendation path, lint/integrity, cost honesty) it contains no assertion, never exits nonzero, and never touches doctor code even though computeRecommendations is exported; cat20's grounding axis is trivially satisfied because the runner injects close/far slugs into every idea line before asking the judge whether ideas cite slugs, and brainstorm errors still get judged (empty ideas string) and averaged into headline means. Minor: gbrain_version is always 'unknown' in all receipts ('gbrain/package.json' not in the export map), cat21's receipt overstates files_ingested and its header claims tree-sitter chunking it doesn't do, cat19's delta reports 0 when unmeasurable. Three improvements proposed: receipt-level ingest/embed/degraded verification (cat18 family), judging only the shipped passes-filtered idea set without truncation (cat20), plus the fs-based version read.

findings.verifier_note: Lines 156-162 match verbatim (line 160 is `foundRelAt10++;` inside the per-row loop). gbrain returns chunk-level SearchResult rows and dedup caps at MAX_PER_PAGE = 2 (verified at /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/src/core/search/dedup.ts:24 and capPerPage at dedup.ts:165-179), so the same slug can appear twice in the top 10; each occurrence increments the numerator while totalRelevant (line 154) counts the slug once. recall_at_10 = foundRelAt10/totalRelevant (line 177) is inflated and can exceed 1.0 (e.g. relSet of size 1 with 2 chunks in top 10 gives 2/1 for that query).
findings.title: Recall@10 numerator counts duplicate chunk rows per relevant page; recall can exceed 100%
findings.evidence: Lines 156-162: `for (let i = 0; i < results.length; i++) { const slug = results[i].slug; if (relSet.has(slug)) { bestRank = Math.min(bestRank, i + 1); foundRelAt10++; } }` — hybridSearch returns chunk-level rows and gbrain's dedup keeps up to 2 chunks per page (MAX_PER_PAGE = 2 in gbrain src/core/search/dedup.ts:24), so one relevant page appearing as 2 chunks in the top 10 increments foundRelAt10 twice while totalRelevant counts it once. recall_at_10 = foundRelAt10/totalRelevant (line 177) is inflated and can exceed 1.0.
findings.suggested_fix: Count distinct matched slugs: `const found = new Set(results.map(r => r.slug).filter(s => relSet.has(s))); foundRelAt10 += found.size;` (and derive bestRank from the first index whose slug is in relSet).
findings.status_note: cat18 recall no longer counts duplicate chunk rows: scoreQuery() page-normalizes via metrics.ts uniqueInOrder then scores with recallAtK/reciprocalRank on distinct page ids; chunk fetch widened to 30 so top-10 PAGES are measured (gbrain dedup keeps <=2 chunks/page).

Default PROVIDERS includes 'zeroentropy' (line 64) so a full run has ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY set process-wide, meaning OpenAI/Voyage cells are reranked too, and query timing (lines 138-148) includes rerank HTTP latency. cat18b:10 does claim 'Cat 18 (parent) ran the no-reranker baseline', which this contradicts.
findings.title: Every 'embedding provider' cell silently runs the ZeroEntropy zerank-2 reranker (default balanced mode), so the A/B does not measure embedders
findings.evidence: Line 141 calls `hybridSearch(engine, q.text, { limit: 10 } as any)` with no mode/reranker config and the runner never calls engine.setConfig. gbrain's default search mode is 'balanced' (src/core/search/mode.ts:502) whose bundle sets `reranker_enabled: true, reranker_model: 'zeroentropyai:zerank-2'` (mode.ts:400-401, ai/defaults.ts:73). Since ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY must be set for the zeroentropy cell, the OpenAI and Voyage cells also get their top-25 reshuffled by ZE's cross-encoder (ZE's own claim: 60% of top-1 reshuffled), and mean_query_ms includes rerank HTTP latency. This contradicts the file header ('how do OpenAI, Voyage, and ZeroEntropy rank against the same query set') and cat18b's header claim that 'Cat 18 (parent) ran the no-reranker baseline'.

findings.verifier_note: Lines 110-117 confirmed: rerank cells set search.mode='tokenmax', baseline cells set 'balanced' plus reranker.enabled toggles. Verified in mode.ts bundles: tokenmax vs balanced also flips expansion (true vs false, lines 452 vs 390), tokenBudget (undefined vs 12000, 451 vs 389), searchLimit (50 vs 25, 453 vs 391), contextual_retrieval ('per_chunk_synopsis' vs 'title', 489 vs 433), and reranker_top_n_in (50 vs 25). Correction: two claimed flips are wrong — relationalRetrieval and autocut are ON in BOTH balanced and tokenmax (mode.ts:436/439 and 492/494); they differ only vs conservative. The core defect stands: the ± pair delta measures a bundle change (notably query expansion and 2x candidate limit), not zerank-2 alone, so cell names and the header misattribute the effect.
findings.title: '± reranker' axis is confounded with a full mode-bundle switch (balanced vs tokenmax)
findings.evidence: Lines 110-117: rerank cells run `engine.setConfig('search.mode', 'tokenmax')` while baseline cells run `engine.setConfig('search.mode', 'balanced')` plus reranker.enabled true/false. In gbrain's mode bundles (src/core/search/mode.ts:383-501), tokenmax vs balanced also flips query expansion (off for balanced, on for tokenmax), token budget, contextual retrieval tier ('title' vs 'per_chunk_synopsis'), relational recall, autocut, and searchLimit. So the delta between 'voyage-1024' and 'voyage-1024+rerank' measures the whole bundle change, not zerank-2 — the file header ('adds zerank-2 on top of each') and cell names misattribute the effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold search.mode constant across the ± pairs (e.g. balanced for both) and toggle only search.reranker.enabled/model, or add explicit mode cells so the reranker delta is isolable.

units.unit_summary: Audited cats 22-25 runners end-to-end against gbrain v0.47.6.0 source (export map, importFromContent/hybridSearch/runThink/resolvePhantomCanonical/findTrajectory signatures, facts-fence format, PGLite engine SQL). All imports resolve and signatures match. Headline finding (critical): cat25's trajectory A/B is a no-op — the seeded '## Facts' tables use a non-canonical format with no fence markers, and importFromContent never reconciles facts into the DB (only the extract_facts cycle phase does), so findTrajectory always returns 0 points and both arms send identical prompts; the published wave-vs-baseline delta is sampling noise. Four majors: cat25 folds judge/think errors into score 0 with no error accounting; cat22's isolation probes pass vacuously on empty results, hardcode getPage totals, and skip rows missing source_id; cat24 labels one importFromContent code path as '5 ingestion paths tested'; cat23's phantoms are full canonical tails that gbrain's prefix expansion (`dir/token-%`) structurally cannot match, so the eval never tests the bare-name resolution the resolver was built for. Minors: cat22 claims traverseGraph coverage without a probe and its 'force keyword-only'/'hermetic' claims are false when OPENAI_API_KEY is set (invalid detail:'normal' opt); cat23 swallows resolver exceptions (a throw on an expected-null phantom counts as correct); cat25 header claims 6 probes/Sonnet vs 2 probes/opus-fallback. Three improvements: pass/fail booleans in cat23/cat24 receipts (cat24 dedup also passes vacuously when the first import failed), judge determinism + sample size for cat25, and using the exported gbrain/think subpath instead of a deep node_modules path. cat22's error probes correctly fail-closed (leaked=-1 breaks isolation_clean); cat24's column detection, provenance opts, and executeRaw row-shape usage all check out against gbrain.

findings.verifier_note: Full chain verified. Probe pages (lines 52-63, 75-85) have a bare '## Facts' markdown table with columns |since|claim|metric|value|unit|period| and no fence markers; parseFactsFence (gbrain facts-fence.ts:170-179) returns {facts: []} when '<!--- gbrain:facts:begin -->' is absent, and the canonical column set differs anyway. importFromContent (called at cat25 line 172) never writes the facts DB table — grep of import-file.ts finds no facts insert; it only touches the markdown fence layer (parse/render/restore at import-file.ts:51,161). Facts-DB population happens only in the extract_facts cycle phase (cycle/extract-facts.ts ~505-525) or the put_page op backstop (ops/pages.ts:708-709), neither of which the runner invokes. runThink's trajectory path reads only the facts table (pglite-engine/facts.ts:466-527, 'FROM facts ... entity_slug = $2'), and think/index.ts:652 'if (boundedPoints.length === 0) return null;' leaves trajectoryBlock '' so line 702 omits it — withTrajectory true/false produce byte-identical prompts. The published cat25 row (docs/benchmarks/2026-05-23-v0.40.6.0-snapshot.md:172, 'wave 10/10 vs baseline 9.5/10, wave wins 1-0-1') is therefore LLM sampling noise. One citation slip: the 'derived index reconciled by extract_facts' statement lives in facts-fence.ts:4-6, not extract-facts.ts:512; substance unaffected.
findings.title: Trajectory A/B measures nothing: seeded facts never reach the facts table, so both arms run identical prompts
findings.evidence: Probe pages seed a '## Facts' table shaped `| since | claim | metric | value | unit | period |` (line 58) with no fence markers. gbrain's fence parser (gbrain/src/core/facts-fence.ts) requires `<!--- gbrain:facts:begin -->` / `:end` markers and the column set `| # | claim | kind | confidence | visibility | notability | valid_from | valid_until | source | context | claim_metric | claim_value | claim_unit | claim_period |`, so parseFactsFence finds nothing. Even with a valid fence, `importFromContent` (line 172) never writes facts to the DB — facts-fence.ts states 'The facts DB table is a derived index reconciled by the new extract_facts cycle phase' (gbrain/src/core/cycle/extract-facts.ts:512), and the runner never runs a cycle or the put_page-op backstop (gbrain/src/core/ops/pages.ts:709). runThink's trajectory path reads only the facts table (`engine.findTrajectory` → `FROM facts WHERE entity_slug = $2` in gbrain/src/core/pglite-engine/facts.ts:466-490) and with 0 points `if (boundedPoints.length === 0) return null;` (think/index.ts:652) leaves trajectoryBlock '' — so withTrajectory:true and withTrajectory:false produce byte-identical prompts. The published result ('wave 10/10 vs baseline 9.5/10, wave wins 1-0-1' in docs/benchmarks/2026-05-23-v0.40.6.0-snapshot.md:172) is pure LLM sampling noise.
findings.suggested_fix: Seed facts through a path that actually populates the facts table: either call `engine.insertFact` directly per typed claim (hermetic, deterministic), or write the canonical fence (markers + 14-column header with claim_metric/claim_value/claim_unit/claim_period and valid_from dates) and run the extract_facts cycle phase after import. Then add a pre-flight assertion that `engine.findTrajectory({entitySlug, kind:'all'})` returns >0 points per probe entity, and assert the wave arm's ThinkResult.warnings contains a `TRAJECTORY_INJECTED_N_POINTS` entry — abort the A/B (nonzero exit) if not, so the eval can never silently degenerate to a same-vs-same comparison.
findings.status_note: Rewrote cat25 to seed typed-claim facts directly via engine.insertFact (claim_metric/claim_value/claim_unit/claim_period, dated valid_from, entity_slug) instead of a bare markdown table that never reached the facts table. findings.title: Judge and think errors silently become score 0 and are aggregated as valid A/B data
findings.evidence: judgeAnswer's catch (lines 144-146) returns `{ score: 0, verdict: `judge error: ...` }` for any API failure (invalid key, 429, refusal, non-JSON output → JSON.parse throw at line 142). runThink failures likewise become the literal answer string `error: ...` (lines 180-181, 189-190) which is then judged. The aggregation (lines 219-232: `baselineMean`, `wave_wins: perProbe.filter(p => p.delta > 0).length`, `ties`) treats these zeros as real scores; the Receipt has no error count field, so a run where every judge call failed writes a receipt showing baseline 0.0 vs wave 0.0 with 2 ties — indistinguishable from 'both answers were wrong'.

Line 232 is exactly 'const isolationClean = probes.every(p => p.leaked_results === 0);' and no probe asserts result presence: hybridSearch returning [] gives leaked=0, listPages returning [] gives leaked=0, getPage returning null for every slug gives leaked=0 with total_results hardcoded to PAGES_PER_SOURCE at line 180. findings.title: Isolation probes pass vacuously on empty results or missing source_id; getPage total is hardcoded
findings.evidence: `const isolationClean = probes.every(p => p.leaked_results === 0);` (line 232) — every probe only counts leaks, never asserts presence. If a regression made scoped reads return zero rows (or `getPage` return null for every slug), all probes report leaked=0 and the receipt declares `isolation_clean: true`. The getPage probe even reports `total_results: PAGES_PER_SOURCE` (line 180) regardless of how many lookups actually returned a page. Additionally the hybridSearch leak check `if (srcId && srcId !== scope)` (line 113) skips any result row lacking `source_id` — SearchResult.source_id is optional in gbrain (types.ts:812 'source_id?: string'), so a code path that drops the column would hide leaks entirely. The published verdict 'Provably clean' (docs/benchmarks/2026-05-23-v0.40.6.0-snapshot.md:170) can be produced by an engine that returns nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert expected result counts per probe and fail the probe otherwise: listPages(alpha) must return exactly 20 rows, listPages(alpha+beta) 40, getPage must find all 10 alpha pages (count non-null returns instead of hardcoding total_results), and hybridSearch must return >=1 row. Treat a result row with missing/undefined source_id as a leak (or resolve it via a pages lookup as the line-107 comment claims) rather than skipping it.

findings.verifier_note: Core claim verified, one mechanism detail wrong. PHANTOMS (lines 51-60) are full slug tails ('alice-okafor' etc.) while the docstring (line 13) promises 'unprefixed slugs: alice, bob-c, charlie'. tryPrefixExpansion builds only `${dir}/${token}-%` (gbrain resolve.ts:333), and 'people/alice-okafor-%' cannot LIKE-match 'people/alice-okafor', so the prefix-expansion layer the resolver was built for (resolve.ts:13-22) is structurally excluded and a bare-name phantom is never tested. CORRECTION: the pg_trgm sub-claim is wrong — gbrain's PGLite schema loads pg_trgm (pglite-schema.ts:32 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;', engine.ts:1459 'Both engines support pg_trgm (PGLite 0.3+)'), and resolvePhantomCanonical tries tryFuzzyMatch FIRST (resolve.ts:241-242), which CAN resolve full-tail phantoms via title similarity. That is what the published '1/7 resolved' shows (almost certainly 'foundry-labs', where 'companies/foundry-labs' sorts before the phantom at tied score in ORDER BY score DESC, slug ASC; the other 4 valid phantoms lose the tiebreak to their own self-match, which resolvePhantomCanonical rejects at line 242 and then gives up without trying rows[1]). So 'every valid phantom is structurally unresolvable' is overstated, but the published number does measure fixture shape + alphabetical tiebreak accidents, not the designed bare-name resolver capability — the defect stands.
findings.title: Phantom fixtures are full canonical tails, which prefix expansion can never match; the designed bare-name case is untested
findings.evidence: PHANTOMS (lines 51-60) use full slug tails like `{ phantom_slug: 'alice-okafor', expected_canonical: 'people/alice-okafor' }`, while the file's own docstring (line 13) says phantoms are 'unprefixed slugs: alice, bob-c, charlie, etc.'. gbrain's tryPrefixExpansion builds only the pattern `${dir}/${token}-%` (gbrain/src/core/entities/resolve.ts:333: `const pattern = `${dir}/${token}-%`;`) — 'people/alice-okafor-%' cannot match 'people/alice-okafor', so on PGLite (no pg_trgm; tryFuzzyMatch's similarity() query throws and is swallowed at resolve.ts:443) every valid phantom is structurally unresolvable no matter how good the resolver is. Meanwhile a bare-name phantom 'alice' WOULD resolve via 'people/alice-%' → 'people/alice-okafor' — the exact capability the resolver was built for (resolve.ts:14-22) — and it is never tested. The published '1/7 resolved, 4/7 missed' (docs/benchmarks/...snapshot.md:171) measures fixture shape, not resolver quality.

findings.verifier_note: Verified. The catch at lines 102-104 ('// best-effort') leaves resolved=null on any throw. The correctness filter (lines 131-134) counts expected_canonical===null && resolved_canonical===null as correct, so a resolver crash on 'team'/'something-random' inflates redirects_correct; a crash on a valid phantom is recorded as outcome 'unresolved' (lines 108-109) and counted in redirects_missing, with no error field on PhantomCase (lines 32-37) to distinguish it. The finding's own reachability caveat is accurate: gbrain's tryFuzzyMatch and tryPrefixExpansion catch SQL errors internally (resolve.ts:443-446, 376-380), so today the throw path is mostly unreachable, but the misreporting is real whenever it fires.
findings.title: Resolver exceptions swallowed; a throw on an expected-null phantom counts as correct
findings.evidence: `try { resolved = await resolvePhantomCanonical(...) } catch (e: any) { // best-effort }` (lines 100-104) leaves `resolved = null` on any throw. The correctness filter (lines 131-134) counts `expected_canonical === null && resolved_canonical === null` as correct, so an engine-level crash on 'team'/'something-random' inflates redirects_correct, and crashes on valid phantoms are recorded as 'unresolved'/'missed valid' with no error field in PhantomCase — errors are indistinguishable from genuine resolver misses in the receipt. (Low reachability today since gbrain's tryFuzzyMatch/tryPrefixExpansion catch SQL errors internally, but the receipt can misreport whenever it fires.)
findings.suggested_fix: Record the caught error message on the PhantomCase (e.g. `error?: string`), add an 'error' outcome distinct from 'unresolved', exclude errored cases from redirects_correct, and surface an error count in the receipt/scorecard.

units.unit_summary: Audited cats 26-29 (4 runner files) against the local gbrain v0.47.6.0 checkout, verifying every import subpath, symbol signature, config key, and table schema in gbrain source. cat26 is effectively a fake eval twice over: it sets the CR mode under 'contextual_retrieval' while gbrain only reads 'search.contextual_retrieval' (all three modes run at the balanced default 'title'), and Recall@10 over a 3-page corpus (dedup caps 2 chunks/page, max 6 results) is structurally 100%, so every delta is 0 and best_mode deterministically reports 'none'. cat27 claims 'Hermetic. No API keys' but seeds via importFromContent with embeddings on, which throws without OPENAI_API_KEY; the per-probe catch then drops errored probes from the aggregate denominator and the run exits 0 with an empty-but-plausible scorecard. Its nDCG also scores duplicate chunk-level slugs (MAX_PER_PAGE=2), allowing nDCG > 1.0. cat28's 'parallel' pass is Promise.all over in-process single-threaded PGLite (does not mirror the v0.40.6 worker pool it claims), measured once with serial-first order so one-time WASM warmup inflates the headline speedup; the advertised per-source setup overhead is computed then discarded. cat29's LLM judge is unblinded (the prompt labels answers 'search'/'think'), judge API failures score 0 and silently flip win counts, think actually runs on the Opus deep-tier default rather than the claimed Sonnet, and golds contain no ground-truth values so hallucinated specifics pass. Cross-cutting: all four runners import 'gbrain/package.json', which is not in gbrain's export map, so gbrain_version is always 'unknown' in receipts. Scoring formulas otherwise check out (cat27 DCG/ideal-DCG math, cat26 recall denominators, cat29 win/tie counts), and the seeded links/sources SQL matches the PGLite schema, sessionPrefix matches the chat/... slug shapes, and hybridSearch/runThink/importFromContent/extractEntityRefs are all called with valid signatures.

findings.verifier_note: The code-level facts are accurate (ndcgAtK, defined at line 157, counts every occurrence with gain 1 against an ideal built from relevant.length=1; search/dedup.ts:24 MAX_PER_PAGE=2 permits 2 chunks per page), but the described consequence cannot occur with the shipped probes. Every probe body is 10-40 words, far under chunkText's 300-word single-chunk threshold (chunkers/recursive.ts:113-117), with no timeline or code fences, so each page produces exactly one chunk. Fusion is chunk-keyed (hybrid.ts:1992-2066), applyGraphSignals only rescores in place (graph-signals.ts:289, returns void), and dedup layer 2 removes identical-text duplicates, so a slug cannot appear twice in the ranked list and nDCG stays ≤ 1.0. This is at most a latent hazard if future probes add 300+ word pages; it does not contaminate current baseline-vs-wave deltas.
findings.title: nDCG computed over chunk-level slug list with duplicates; can exceed 1.0
findings.evidence: Line 329 `baseline.map((r: any) => r.slug)` keeps one entry per SearchResult, and gbrain's dedup allows up to 2 chunks per page (dedup.ts:24 `MAX_PER_PAGE = 2`), so the same slug can appear twice in the ranked list. ndcgAtK (line 159) maps every occurrence to gain 1 while the ideal DCG is built from `relevant.length` = 1 (line 161), so a gold page at ranks 1 and 2 scores dcg([1,1])/dcg([1]) = 1.63. Deltas between baseline and wave can then reflect duplicate-chunk counts rather than page ranking.

findings.title: Judge API failure is scored as 0 and silently folded into means and win counts
findings.evidence: Lines 136-138: `catch (e) { return { score: 0, verdict: 'judge error: ...' }; }`. A transient Haiku 429/timeout on one side scores that side 0, flipping `think_wins` (line 204) and dragging `search_mean_score`/`think_mean_score` (lines 217-218). The aggregate receipt has no judge-error counter, so a run with judge failures is indistinguishable from a run where answers genuinely scored 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Retry the judge call with backoff; if it still fails, exclude the question from aggregates (or mark it `judge_failed: true` and report a `judge_errors` count in the receipt) instead of scoring 0.
findings.status_note: Judge API failures and judge_failed verdicts now throw JudgeFailure -> acc.error(qid,'judge',...) per the probe-accounting policy: the question is EXCLUDED from means (search/think scores null, judged-only aggregates), recorded in receipt errors[], capped, and publishable flips false on smoke runs —

findings.verifier_note: Header lines 10-11 say 'Cost: ~$3 — one Sonnet think call per question' and line 168 sets chat_model in configureGateway, but runThink resolves via resolveModel(engine, { configKey: 'models.think', tier: 'deep', fallback: 'opus' }) (think/index.ts:493-498). resolveModelDetailed (model-config.ts:368-441) reads CLI flag, engine config keys, GBRAIN_MODEL env, then the key-aware tier default — never gateway state. On this fresh PGLite brain with isolated GBRAIN_HOME, none of steps 1-6 fire; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present (the judge requires it), so resolveTierDefault returns TIER_DEFAULTS.deep = 'anthropic:claude-opus-4-7' (model-config.ts:93, 147), and think/index.ts:734/786 uses that model for the synthesis call. Cost understated and the measured model uncontrolled, as claimed.
findings.title: Think runs on Opus by default, not the Sonnet the header and gateway config claim
findings.evidence: Header (lines 10-12) says 'Cost: ~$3 — one Sonnet think call per question' and line 168 sets `chat_model: 'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6'` in configureGateway. But runThink resolves its model via `resolveModel(engine, { configKey: 'models.think', tier: 'deep', fallback: 'opus' })` (think/index.ts:493-498), which never consults the gateway chat_model; on this fresh brain with isolated GBRAIN_HOME it falls to TIER_DEFAULTS.deep = 'anthropic:claude-opus-4-7' (model-config.ts:93). So the eval silently runs Opus: cost is understated and the measured 'think' quality is tied to an uncontrolled model choice.

findings.verifier_note: Line 36 imports runThink from '../../node_modules/gbrain/src/core/think/index.ts' while gbrain's exports map publishes "./think": "./src/core/think/index.ts" (gbrain package.json line 26). The relative path is layout-fragile and resolves as a different module specifier than the 'gbrain/*' subpath imports used elsewhere in the same file, so a second module instance (separate module-level state) is possible. 'gbrain/think' is the correct drop-in.
findings.title: Deep node_modules path import bypasses the published 'gbrain/think' subpath export
findings.evidence: Line 36: `import { runThink } from '../../node_modules/gbrain/src/core/think/index.ts';`. gbrain's export map already publishes `"./think": "./src/core/think/index.ts"` (gbrain package.json line 26). The relative path breaks if the file moves, if the package layout changes, or under package managers with non-flat node_modules, and it can load a second module instance alongside 'gbrain/*' imports.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with `import { runThink } from 'gbrain/think';`.
findings.status_note: Deep node_modules path import replaced with the published subpath export: import { runThink, type ThinkResponse } from 'gbrain/think'.

The cited sibling sites check out exactly: cat27-graph-signals.ts:410, cat28-federated-sync-latency.ts:128, cat29-think-vs-search.ts:213, and 17 runner files total use the pattern (so '8+ other runners' is accurate). findings.title: gbrain_version is always 'unknown': 'gbrain/package.json' is not in the export map
findings.evidence: Line 152 `await import('gbrain/package.json' as any)` — gbrain's package.json defines an "exports" map (lines 9-32) that does not include './package.json', so subpath resolution fails (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED semantics), the catch at line 154 swallows it, and every receipt records gbrain_version: 'unknown'. Same pattern at cat27:410, cat28:128, cat29:213 (and 8+ other runners), so no receipt in this unit can be tied to the gbrain commit it measured.

findings.verifier_note: All five golds (lines 50-76) are meta-descriptions: line 59 asks for 'approximate values' without stating them; line 74 says 'reports the 2026-04-10 ARR value' without the value. The judge prompt (110-124) receives only question + gold + answer, and the synthetic corpus does contain concrete ARR facts the golds omit (e.g. eval/data/synthetic-v1/companies/*.md Facts fences: '2026-04-10 | ARR is $1458K | arr | 1457501'). A think answer inventing a plausible figure in the right date order is unverifiable by the judge and can score 10, exactly as claimed.
findings.title: Gold answers contain no ground-truth values, so the judge cannot detect hallucinated specifics
findings.evidence: Every gold is a meta-description of what a good answer should do, not the facts themselves — e.g. line 59: 'seeds Acme AI 0 with 3 Facts-fence ARR readings on 3 different dates... should report the trajectory in order, including approximate values' (values never stated), line 74: 'A correct answer either reports the 2026-04-10 ARR value...' (value never stated). The judge scores 'accuracy' (line 116) against this, so a think answer that invents an ARR of $99M in the right date order can score 10 while being wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the corpus loader (or a build step) extract the actual seeded values (ARR numbers, attendee slugs, top-linked concepts) into each question's gold so the judge verifies concrete facts; alternatively pass the relevant gold pages' Facts fences to the judge as ground-truth context.
findings.status_note: buildQuestions() now extracts the ACTUAL seeded values from the committed corpus at runtime (deterministic, drift-proof): real ARR readings with values and dates from the Facts fences (companies/acme-co-0, cobalt-labs-16 — also fixing the old questions' references to nonexistent entities 'Acme AI 0'

units.unit_summary: Audited the 5 SkillOpt/BrainBench runners (cat30-34) and the skillopt-v1 generator against the local gbrain v0.47.6.0 checkout. The core machinery is genuine: reflectMode/optimizerMode/disableValidationGate are real orchestrator knobs (orchestrator.ts:384/495/546), so cat31's ablation actually removes what it names; cat32's reward-hacking design is sound (rule judge trivially gameable, LLM held-out judge resolves per-task judge.model so the Sonnet judge is used consistently, and the orchestrator's held-out gate really blocks at checkpoint acceptance); scoreSkillOnTasks/loadHeldOut/runSkillOpt signatures all match; cat34's CLI flags, metric names, and result schema all conform to the published contract; all four seed-* fixture dirs exist with 15 bench + 6 held-out rows, disjoint task_ids, valid judge ops. Real defects found: (1) cat33's B-pre validity gate can never fail because PairResult.error is never assigned while optimizeOn swallows runSkillOpt errors — the validity mode measures nothing; (2) cat31 counts errored trials as heldout=0, which makes the D_no_gate arm of the gate easier to pass on silent failure; (3) cat33 computes the Y-optimized ceiling and transfer_ratio but never gates on the documented \"reasonable band\" condition (and the 1e-6 denominator clamp can emit ratios of ~500000); (4) cat34 parses a stale result.json from a prior run when the subprocess fails to write; plus minor issues (unseeded bootstrap p-value RNG, gbrain_version always 'unknown' because './package.json' is not exported, cat31 header describing an unimplemented gate, leaked tmpdir homes). Highest-value improvements: give held-out.jsonl an independent judge (currently byte-identical checks to the training bench, so cat30/cat33 held-out only tests topic transfer), validate result_schema_version in cat34, and replace deep node_modules/src imports with a proper gbrain subpath export.

findings.verifier_note: Exact as claimed. `error?: string` (line 84) is never assigned anywhere in the file; runPair's return (lines 136-140) omits it. optimizeOn's catch (lines 101-104) swallows runSkillOpt failures and returns the seed with outcome 'errored', which is only written to stderr (line 116) and never stored in PairResult. So `results.every((r) => !r.error)` at line 159 is vacuously true and SKILLOPT_BPRE=1 exits 0 despite an errored optimize. Minor scope note: if scoreSkillOnTasks itself throws, main rejects and the process exits nonzero, so only runSkillOpt-path failures pass silently — which is exactly the 'skillopt plumbing' the finding describes.
findings.title: B-pre validity gate can never fail: PairResult.error is declared but never set
findings.evidence: Line 159: `? results.every((r) => !r.error) // validity: ran end-to-end`. But `runPair` returns (lines 136-140) `{ seed, x, y, seed_on_y, xopt_on_y, yopt_on_y, transfer_lift, transfer_ratio, transferred, cost_usd }` — the `error?: string` field (line 84) is never assigned anywhere. When `runSkillOpt` throws, `optimizeOn` swallows it (lines 101-104: `catch ... return { best: seedBody, cost: 0, outcome: 'errored' }`) and even the `outcome: 'errored'` string is only logged to stderr (line 116), never stored in the result. So SKILLOPT_BPRE=1 exits 0 (PASS) even when the skillopt plumbing errored — exactly what the validity mode exists to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate optimizeOn's outcome into PairResult (e.g. `x_outcome: xopt.outcome`, set `error` when outcome === 'errored') and gate B-pre on `results.every((r) => !r.error && r.x_outcome !== 'errored')`, mirroring cat30's catch (cat30 line 128 sets `error` and cat30's B-pre gate checks `!r.error`).

findings.verifier_note: Line 101 returns `{ heldout: 0, sel: 0, cost: 0, outcome: 'errored' }` from the catch; meanHeldout (line 132) averages all trials with no exclusion. Full-mode gate (lines 141, 159-162) is `loopLifts && (A >= D - 0.05)`, so an errored D_no_gate trial drags D toward 0 and makes gateIsFree trivially true. `outcome === 'errored'` is only consulted in BPRE mode (line 139); in full mode it is only echoed into the receipt's per-trial array (line 174) without affecting gatePass. Consequence is real.
findings.title: Errored trials counted as heldout=0; an error in the D_no_gate config silently makes the gate easier to pass
findings.evidence: Line 101: `return { heldout: 0, sel: 0, cost: 0, outcome: 'errored' };` — the catch swallows any runSkillOpt/scoreSkillOnTasks failure and records score 0. Those zeros flow into `meanHeldout` (line 132) with no exclusion. The full-mode gate (lines 141, 161-162) is `gateIsFree = A >= D - GATE_EPS`, so a crashed D_no_gate trial (heldout 0) drags D down and makes the "gate is free insurance" condition trivially true. Outcome 'errored' is checked only in BPRE mode (line 139); in full mode it is recorded in the receipt but never affects gatePass.

findings.verifier_note: Docstring lines 17-21 promise a two-clause gate (lift > margin AND within a band of Y-optimized, citing codex r2 #12). The implemented full-mode gate (line 160) is only `transferred >= ceil(0.75 * pairs)` where transferred = transfer_lift > 0.05 (line 139). The Y-optimize ceiling run is executed and paid for (lines 124-128) and transfer_ratio is computed (lines 132-133) but appears in no pass/fail decision. The 1e-6 denominator clamp at line 132 means yoptOnY <= seedOnY yields absurd ratios (e.g. 0.5/1e-6 = 500000) in the receipt. All exact.
findings.title: Documented "within a reasonable band of Y-optimized" gate condition never implemented; transfer_ratio computed then ignored (and can explode)
findings.evidence: Docstring lines 17-21: "Gate: X-optimized beats the unoptimized seed on Y (transfer lift > margin) on >= ceil(0.75 * pairs), AND lands within a reasonable band of Y-optimized. Per codex r2 #12 the seed-vs-Xopt comparison alone could just show the edit is generically useful; the Y-optimized ceiling distinguishes 'transferred' from 'trivially better'." The implemented gate (line 160) is only `transferred >= Math.ceil(results.length * 0.75)` where `transferred = transferLift > MARGIN` (line 139). The Y-optimized ceiling run is paid for (line 126) and `transfer_ratio` is computed (lines 132-133) but never used in any pass/fail decision. Also `const denom = Math.max(1e-6, yoptOnY - seedOnY)` (line 132) means a ceiling at-or-below the floor yields ratios like 0.5/1e-6 = 500000 in the receipt.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the documented second clause, e.g. `transferred = transferLift > MARGIN && transferRatio >= 0.5` (or a band vs yopt_on_y), and clamp/NaN-guard the ratio when `yoptOnY - seedOnY` is at or below noise (report null instead of a 1e-6-denominator value). Otherwise fix the docstring to say the ceiling is informational only.

findings.verifier_note: outFile is the fixed path eval/reports/cat34-brainbench-memory/result.json (line 75; eval/reports/ is gitignored and persists between runs). The only failure detection is `!existsSync(outFile)` at line 86 — nothing deletes the artifact before Bun.spawnSync at line 84. If the subprocess exits without writing, a result.json from an earlier successful run passes the check and lines 90-141 rebuild receipt.json/scorecard.md from the stale document with a fresh timestamp (line 104) and the current checkout's package.json version (line 94). The finding correctly notes the subprocess exit code is still propagated (lines 108, 129, 143), but the published artifacts mislabel old cells/fixtures_hash as a new run.
findings.title: Stale result.json from a previous run is parsed as the current run's result when the subprocess fails to write
findings.evidence: Line 75 fixes `outFile = resolve(REPORT_DIR, 'result.json')` (constant name, persistent gitignored dir). Line 86: `if (!existsSync(outFile))` is the only failure detection. If `gbrain eval brainbench` exits without writing (e.g. exit 2 on a flag/fixture error against an older checkout), a result.json left by an earlier successful run satisfies `existsSync`, and lines 90-141 rebuild receipt.json and scorecard.md from the STALE document with a fresh `timestamp: new Date().toISOString()` (line 104) and the CURRENT repo's `gbrain_version` (line 94). The exit code is still propagated, but the published artifacts show old cells/fixtures_hash labeled as a new run.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the artifact before spawning (`rmSync(outFile, { force: true })`) or write to a run-unique temp path, and treat `exitCode !== 0 && exitCode !== 1` as no-result even if the file exists.

findings.verifier_note: Line 75 resamples with bare Math.random and no seed; the resulting p-value is persisted in the receipt as paired_bootstrap_p_A_vs_C (line 176), so identical trial scores produce different receipts run-to-run. The generator (eval/generators/skillopt-v1-gen.ts line 12) does advertise 'Deterministic (no randomness) so re-running is stable' as a corpus property. Correctly scoped as minor: pAvsC is not used in gatePass (lines 136-163), so scores/exit code are unaffected.
findings.title: Unseeded Math.random in paired-bootstrap p-value makes the reported statistic non-reproducible
findings.evidence: Line 75: `for (let i = 0; i < deltas.length; i++) sum += deltas[Math.floor(Math.random() * deltas.length)]!;` — the p-value written to the receipt as `paired_bootstrap_p_A_vs_C` (line 176) differs run-to-run even for identical trial scores. The generator file advertises determinism as a corpus property, and the receipt is the persisted comparison artifact. (Not gated, so scores are unaffected.)
findings.suggested_fix: Use a small seeded PRNG (e.g. mulberry32 with a fixed seed recorded in the receipt) so the receipt's p-value is reproducible from the trial scores.
findings.status_note: pairedBootstrapPValue now takes an injectable RNG defaulting to mulberry32(BOOTSTRAP_SEED=0x5eed31); the runner passes the seeded PRNG explicitly and records bootstrap_seed in receipt resolved_config. Deltas are computed over CLEAN A/C trial pairs only.

findings.evidence: Line 174: `const pkg = await import('gbrain/package.json' as any);` inside try/catch with fallback 'unknown'. /home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/package.json has an "exports" map whose keys are ['.', './engine', ..., './core/guardrails'] with NO './package.json' entry, so Node/Bun exports encapsulation rejects the subpath and the catch fires every time. Implemented full-mode gate (lines 159-162) is only lift-over-seed-floor (A - seedHeldout > 0.3) plus A >= D - 0.05. findings.title: File header describes a gate the code does not implement (A>C and the D-sel-overfit check)
findings.evidence: Docstring lines 22-24: "Gate: A > {C one-shot, D no-gate} on held-out (the loop + the gate each earn their cost), AND D shows HIGHER sel but LOWER/EQUAL held-out than A (the gate prevents overfit — the core safety story)." A reader of the header believes a stronger claim was tested than actually was.

findings.verifier_note: Generator lines 130-131 write benchmark.jsonl and held-out.jsonl from the same seed.checks array for every seed, and the committed fixtures confirm it: seed-missing-structure bm-001 and hd-001 both carry [{op:'section_present',arg:'Key Risks'},{op:'regex',arg:'[Cc]onfidence\\s*[:=]'}]. Only task_id prefix and topic wording differ. cat30's headline (lines 4-5, 'BETTER on a HELD-OUT set it was never optimized against') and cat33's transfer gate therefore reward any edit that satisfies the exact trained-on rule strings; cat32 Part A demonstrates a form-only skill scores high on such rule judges while an LLM quality judge scores it low. The generator's own claim of an 'independent gate' (line 6) rests on disjoint task_ids only. Genuine design weakness, correctly filed as improvement.
findings.title: Held-out sets use byte-identical judge checks to the training benchmark, so cat30/cat33 'held-out' only tests topic transfer
findings.evidence: Line 130-131: `writeFileSync(join(dir, 'benchmark.jsonl'), jsonl('bm', seed.benchTopics, verb, seed.checks)); writeFileSync(join(dir, 'held-out.jsonl'), jsonl('hd', seed.heldTopics, verb, seed.checks));` — same `seed.checks` array for both (confirmed in the committed fixtures: seed-missing-structure bench and held-out rows both carry `{op:'section_present',arg:'Key Risks'},{op:'regex',arg:'[Cc]onfidence...'}`). cat30's headline ("BETTER on a HELD-OUT set it was never optimized against", line 4-5) and cat33's transfer gate therefore reward any edit satisfying the exact rule the optimizer trained on — a form-only edit (the very hack cat32 demonstrates scores 1.0 on rule judges) transfers by construction. Only the topic wording is held out.
findings.suggested_fix: Give held-out.jsonl an independent judge — an LLM quality rubric like cat32's QUALITY_RUBRIC, or at minimum differently-phrased/stricter rule checks — so cat30's improvement delta and cat33's transfer lift measure genuine quality transfer rather than replication of the trained-on rule strings.
findings.status_note: Held-out sets now carry differentiated, stricter judge checks per seed (documented in the generator header): missing-structure requires a substantive risk bullet under the heading + a same-line stated confidence level; verbose gets a 900-char cap + 200-char substance floor; no-brain-first adds min_c

units.unit_summary: Audited the PrecisionMemBench unit (13 files) read-only. The vendored scorer (baseAdapter.ts, buildRetrievalReport.ts, runCases.ts, belief.ts) is internally sound: precision/recall/pinnedCoverage math matches the parity tests, p50/p95 use correct nearest-rank index math, pass-type classification and per-category means check out, and the committed instrument JSON's separatrix numbers (30/32=94%, gaps 0.602 vs 0.569) match both the published .md §7 and the rationale comment in gbrain's return-policy.ts. All gbrain imports were verified against v0.47.6.0: subpath exports exist, and hybridSearch/SearchOpts (limit, sourceIds, useCache, adaptiveReturn{enabled,entityMax,otherMax}), classifyQueryIntent, runThink({question,model,rounds})→citations[].page_slug, importFromContent(engine, slug, content, {sourceId,noEmbed}), softDeletePage(slug,{sourceId}), and configureGateway(AIGatewayConfig) are all called compatibly. The committed report JSONs match the .md's headline/§5 tables and p50 claims. Seven findings: (1) major — seed.ts soft-deletes beliefs using the fixture's ground-truth `superseded_by` field, a signal the upstream /add contract never gives leaderboard providers, converting supersession failures into passes and removing precision-polluting aliases index-wide; (2) major — the runner accepts any --mode/--fidelity string uncast-validated, so a typo (e.g. `--mode gbrain-adaptive-tight`, matching a committed artifact name) silently runs plain hybrid published under the wrong label; (3) major — report filename/payload omit entityMax/otherMax/limit, so same-day cap variants overwrite each other (the two committed adaptive JSONs share the identical embedded provider string and were disambiguated by hand-renaming); (4) minor — --json mode leaves gbrain's init/seed logging unsilenced on the same stdout as the JSON payload; (5) minor — the instrument's separatrix capture keys by query text, which collides on the fixture's 4 duplicated queries (harmless today, silently corrupting under future fixtures); plus 2 improvements (partial-run rows in the leaderboard table lack an n caveat; the cliff prototype's score normalization breaks on negative rerank scores). No metric-math, threshold, or fake-eval defects found in the scorer itself.

findings.verifier_note: Every evidence link holds. seed.ts:117-120 soft-deletes on the fixture's ground-truth superseded_by; gbrain search then hides those pages (gbrain sql-ranking.ts:196 'deleted_at IS NULL', softDeletePage at postgres-engine.ts:867). The vendored upstream seed contract (baseAdapter.ts:142-151) sends only {text, user_id, metadata:{beliefId, scope}, aliases} — no supersession field — so leaderboard systems (LEADERBOARD hardcoded at runner lines 48-57, supermemory 0.43) only saw in-band prose like 'Previously used TSLint... Replaced by ESLint.' All 4 superseded beliefs exist as claimed and b-sqlalchemy-superseded carries alias 'Postgres'. Consequence is real: for conflict-mongodb-supersedes-sqlalchemy (query 'how's our SQLAlchemy setup these days?', shouldOnlyInclude: []), a live superseded belief would fail the case with precision 0 (runCases.ts:179-191, 260-265); soft-deleted it scores precision null and passes, lifting meanPrecision (nulls are excluded from the mean, buildRetrievalReport.ts:104-118) and passRate. The .md does say 'No benchmark-specific logic' at docs/benchmarks/2026-05-29-precisionmembench.md:69. Caveat for fairness: the mechanism itself is openly documented (seed.ts header lines 10-12, runner header line 13-14, .md §11 'Honest seeding'), so this is a disclosed design choice — but the asymmetry vs the published provider contract is real, unflagged in §9, and the seed branch is literally fixture-state-specific logic, so the finding's core claim stands.
findings.title: Seed path consumes fixture ground-truth `superseded_by` to pre-hide beliefs from gbrain's index, a signal the upstream provider contract never delivers
findings.evidence: seed.ts:117-120: `if (b.superseded_by != null) { await engine.softDeletePage(b._id as string, { sourceId }); softDeleted++; }`. The vendored upstream seeding contract (scorer/baseAdapter.ts:142-151) sends providers only `{ text, user_id, metadata: {beliefId, scope}, aliases }` — no supersession field — so leaderboard systems (supermemory 0.43 etc., hardcoded in eval/runner/precisionmembench.ts:48-57) had to infer supersession from belief text ('Previously used TSLint... Replaced by ESLint.'). gbrain instead gets the harness to remove all 4 superseded beliefs (b-sqlalchemy-superseded, b-narrator-superseded, b-linting-v0, b-linting-v1) from its searchable index at seed time. This flips supersession cases (e.g. conflict-mongodb-supersedes-sqlalchemy, shouldOnlyInclude: []) from precision-0 fails to precision-null passes, and stops superseded beliefs from polluting unrelated cases (b-sqlalchemy-superseded carries alias 'Postgres'), lifting meanPrecision and passRate across the run. The .md claims 'No benchmark-specific logic' (§4) while this branch is exactly fixture-state-specific logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Either detect supersession through gbrain's own pipeline (ingest beliefs in order and let an update/contradiction step soft-delete, or parse the in-band 'Replaced by' text), or keep the shortcut but add a mode that seeds superseded beliefs live (`--supersession in-band`) and report both numbers; at minimum flag the asymmetry in the runner's leaderboard table and §9 caveats instead of only describing the mechanism.
findings.status_note: Removed the seed-time leak: eval/precisionmembench/seed.ts no longer consults ground-truth superseded_by; all 35 beliefs seed live (return renamed to {imported, supersededLive}) so gbrain must exclude superseded beliefs itself. Runner scorecard/payload/receipt state 'superseded seeded LIVE'. Report

findings.verifier_note: Line 75 is a bare cast with no validation. Dispatch (lines 120-132) sends any unrecognized mode into the final else branch: new GbrainBeliefAdapter(engine, mode === 'gbrain-keyword' ? 'keyword' : 'hybrid'), i.e. plain top-K hybrid with adaptiveReturn off (the .md §5 table shows that config at 0.076 precision). provider = `${opts.mode}-${opts.fidelity}` (line 138) and the filename (line 147) then embed the bogus string, e.g. '--mode gbrain-adaptive-tight' would produce exactly 2026-05-30-gbrain-adaptive-tight-body-text.json, the name of a committed artifact. findings.title: Unvalidated --mode: any unknown mode string silently runs plain hybrid but stamps the bogus mode into the provider label, filename, and published payload
findings.evidence: Line 75: `const mode = (get('--mode') ?? 'gbrain-hybrid') as Opts['mode'];` — a bare cast, never validated. The dispatch (lines 121-132) is `if (mode === 'gbrain-think') ... else if (mode === 'gbrain-adaptive') ... else new GbrainBeliefAdapter(engine, mode === 'gbrain-keyword' ? 'keyword' : 'hybrid')`, so e.g. `--mode gbrain-adaptive-tight` (the exact name of the committed artifact docs/benchmarks/2026-05-29-precisionmembench/2026-05-30-gbrain-adaptive-tight-body-text.json) falls into the else branch, runs plain top-K hybrid (~0.076 precision) with adaptiveReturn OFF, and publishes it as `gbrain-adaptive-tight-body-text` via `const provider = \`${opts.mode}-${opts.fidelity}\`` (line 138). Same for `--fidelity`: any value other than the literal 'structured' silently behaves as body-text (seed.ts:98-104) while being embedded in the label.

findings.status_note: parseOpts now iterates argv strictly: --mode whitelisted against MODES (gbrain-hybrid|gbrain-keyword|gbrain-think|gbrain-adaptive), --fidelity against FIDELITIES (body-text|structured), --limit/--entity-max/--other-max validated as integers, unknown flags hard-error. gbrain-keyword still forces noEm

findings.verifier_note: Verified end to end. provider = mode-fidelity only (line 138), reportPath = `${date}-${provider}.json` (line 147), and buildReportPayload writes only {provider, retrieval, cases} (buildRetrievalReport.ts:207-218; ingestion is never passed by this runner). The caps from lines 127-128 appear nowhere in the payload. Committed proof checks out exactly: 2026-05-30-gbrain-adaptive-default-body-text.json (meanPrecision 0.1638) and 2026-05-30-gbrain-adaptive-tight-body-text.json (meanPrecision 0.582) both embed identical "provider": "gbrain-adaptive-body-text" and are distinguishable only by hand-edited filenames the runner cannot produce. findings.title: Report filename and payload omit the run config (entityMax/otherMax/limit/noEmbed), so same-day adaptive runs with different caps silently overwrite each other and published numbers lose provenance
findings.evidence: Line 138: `const provider = \`${opts.mode}-${opts.fidelity}\`;` and line 147: `const reportPath = join(REPORT_DIR, \`${date}-${provider}.json\`);` — the caps passed at lines 127-128 (`adaptiveReturn.entityMax/otherMax`) and `--limit`/`--no-embed` never reach the filename or the payload (buildReportPayload writes only provider/retrieval/cases). Proof in the committed artifacts: docs/benchmarks/2026-05-29-precisionmembench/2026-05-30-gbrain-adaptive-default-body-text.json (prec 0.1638) and ...-tight-body-text.json (prec 0.582) both embed the identical `"provider": "gbrain-adaptive-body-text"` and are distinguishable only by hand-edited filenames; running the documented reproduction commands (md §10, two `--mode gbrain-adaptive` invocations with different caps) on one day clobbers the first JSON. The committed keyword JSON similarly hides that it was a `--limit 10` partial run except via caseCount.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold the resolved run options into both the payload (e.g. `payload.config = { mode, fidelity, limit, noEmbed, entityMax, otherMax, gbrainVersion }`) and the filename (append `-e1-o1` style suffix or a timestamp) so distinct configurations can never collide or lose provenance.

findings.verifier_note: The code fact is accurate (lines 102-105 silence console only when !opts.json), but the claimed consequence — a corrupted stdout stream for `--json | jq` — cannot occur. gbrain's init/import chatter goes exclusively through console.warn/console.error, which write to stderr, not stdout: import-file.ts and pglite-engine.ts contain zero console.log or process.stdout.write calls (all ~20 log sites are console.warn); migrate.ts contains no console.log (its only grep hit, line 5584, is a comment recording that a console.log there was already removed precisely because it polluted `doctor --json`); ai/gateway.ts, config.ts, embedding.ts, embed-retry.ts, utils.ts, guardrails.ts contain none. The only stdout logger reachable in theory is schema-verify.ts's self-heal message (lines 285/294), which fires only when columns are missing — impossible on the freshly created in-memory schema. In --json mode stdout receives exactly one write: the payload at line 153. Piped jq gets a clean stream; the unsilenced chatter lands on stderr, which is at worst cosmetic.
findings.title: --json mode leaves console unsilenced during engine init + seeding, so gbrain migrate/import logs pollute the machine-readable stdout
findings.evidence: Lines 102-105: `if (!opts.json) { console.log = () => {}; console.error = () => {}; }` — silencing is applied only in the human-scorecard path. In `--json` mode, `createBenchEngine()` (schema init/migrations, which log via console) and `seedGbrainEngine` (the 'chatty import/extract logs' the comment at line 99 itself names) run unsilenced, then line 153 prints the JSON payload to the same stdout — so `bun eval/runner/precisionmembench.ts --json | jq` gets a corrupted stream. The guard is inverted relative to the mode that most needs clean stdout.
findings.suggested_fix: Silence console in json mode too (restore just before `origLog(JSON.stringify(payload...))`), or redirect gbrain chatter to stderr and reserve stdout for the payload.
