findings.verifier_note: Verified. The test (lines 259-274) builds evidence via makeEvidence with only structured saw_poison_items: ['poison-001','poison-002']; the strings 'Ignore all previous' and '<TOOL_OUTPUT>' appear nowhere in that evidence object (the only other occurrence of 'Ignore all previous instructions' is line 242 in the separate assertNoRawToolOutput test on a different object). The not.toContain assertions at 272-273 are therefore vacuously true no matter what renderEvidenceForJudge emits.
findings.title: Judge-blinding assertions can't fail: the 'poisonous payload' is never injected into the evidence
findings.evidence: Lines 259-274: the comment says 'Craft poisonous tool-result text (what the bridge WOULD see but judge never does)', but the test only sets structured `saw_poison_items: ['poison-001', 'poison-002']` and then asserts `expect(rendered).not.toContain('Ignore all previous')` and `not.toContain('<TOOL_OUTPUT>')` — strings that were never placed anywhere in the JudgeEvidence, so these negative assertions are vacuously true regardless of what renderEvidenceForJudge does.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the evidence through the real pipeline: run buildEvidence over an AgentRunResult whose transcript tool_result content contains a sentinel injection payload, then assert the payload string is absent from renderEvidenceForJudge's output while the fixture_ids are present. That makes the blinding test able to fail if a raw-content field is ever added to the contract.
findings.status_note: The blinding test now injects the payload through the REAL pipeline: an AgentRunResult whose transcript tool_result content contains 'Ignore all previous instructions ... <TOOL_OUTPUT>...' (with matched_poison_fixture_ids poison-001/poison-002) goes through cat9's buildEvidence(); the test asserts t

findings.verifier_note: Verified. weightedMean (eval/runner/judge.ts:241-252) sums only over the judge-returned scores, dropping missing criteria from both numerator and denominator; scoreAnswer computes overall = weightedMean(parsed.scores, evidence.rubric) at line 385 and the canonical verdict via verdictFromScore at 389, with no completeness check against evidence.rubric anywhere (parseToolUse lines 268-299 only shape-checks each score entry). A judge returning 1 of 3 criteria with score 5 yields overall_score 5 → 'pass' (threshold 3.5). The weightedMean describe (judge.test.ts:354-390) covers equal weights, weight=2, empty rubric, and unknown criterion_id, but never fewer scores than rubric criteria — exactly as claimed.
findings.title: No coverage for judge omitting rubric criteria — weightedMean silently renormalizes over the returned subset, inflating scores
findings.evidence: weightedMean (eval/runner/judge.ts:241-252) sums only over `scores` the judge returned: `for (const s of scores) { ... totalWeight += w; }` — a criterion missing from the tool_use output is dropped from both numerator and denominator, so a judge that scores only the criteria it liked (e.g. returns 1 of 3 criteria with score 5) yields overall_score 5 and verdict 'pass'. scoreAnswer performs no completeness check against evidence.rubric, and judge.test.ts's weightedMean describe (lines 354-390) tests equal weights, weight=2, empty rubric, and unknown criterion_id — but never fewer scores than rubric criteria.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test where the stub judge returns scores for a strict subset of the rubric and assert the desired behavior (missing criteria treated as score 0, or the response treated as malformed triggering the retry path); then implement that in scoreAnswer/parseToolUse by cross-checking parsed criterion_ids against evidence.rubric.
findings.status_note: judge omission tests added

units.unit_summary: Audited the 10 docs-vs-code files (5 benchmark reports, comparison-systems, both READMEs, RUNBOOK, CHANGELOG) against the runners, adapters, package.json scripts, committed JSON/SVG artifacts, the gbrain checkout (v0.47.6.0), and the live HuggingFace URL. What checks out: all reproduction file paths and CLI flags exist (longmemeval --stratify/--top-k/--adapters, precisionmembench --mode/--entity-max/--other-max, cat30-34 runners, gbrain `eval brainbench` flags, gen.ts/query-new flags, seed 42), all gbrain subpath imports resolve in the export map, the LongMemEval per-type table is arithmetically consistent (misses sum to 488/487/99 of 500), SVG numbers match the prose, most precisionmembench numbers match their committed JSONs, the HF download URL is live, adversarial count is really 22, and adapter names match the registry. Found 12 bugs + 2 improvements: 4 major (eval:run advertised as keyless/offline but requires OPENAI_API_KEY; the LongMemEval warm embed cache claimed 'committed ~150MB' when the cache dir's own README says NOT committed/~700MB/different path; 'shipping = runs in CI and gates releases' with zero CI config and Cats 5/8/9 skipped as programmatic by all.ts; reproduce-from-commit claims while gbrain is pinned to floating #master) and 8 minor doc/artifact mismatches (nonexistent test:eval script, phantom openai dependency, stale 'gitignored' amara-life note, 80 tier-5 queries claimed in metrics but never scored, quick-start stratify command running K=8 vs published K=5, unimplemented 'randomized question order' claim, headline 0.076 vs committed 0.0752 artifact, unqualified SOTA claims contradicting the repo's own comparison table).

findings.verifier_note: README.md:124 says 'no API keys, fully offline' and line 127 runs `bun run eval:run` = eval/runner/multi-adapter.ts (package.json:13). With no --adapter flag the runner instantiates HybridNoGraphAdapter and VectorOnlyAdapter (multi-adapter.ts:485-489); eval/runner/adapters/vector.ts:33 imports embed/embedBatch from 'gbrain/embedding', which routes through gbrain's OpenAI gateway (gbrain/src/core/ai/gateway.ts uses @ai-sdk/openai). The repo's own eval/RUNBOOK.md:7-17 documents that this exact command needs OPENAI_API_KEY. The 'behavior suite' half is also wrong: identity/temporal/adversarial/multimodal/cat34 run via eval:brainbench (eval/runner/all.ts CATEGORIES), not multi-adapter.ts, which is retrieval-only P@5/R@5.
findings.title: BrainBench quick-start claims 'no API keys, fully offline' but eval:run requires OPENAI_API_KEY
findings.evidence: README.md:124 says "**Our own suite (we call it BrainBench; no API keys, fully offline):**" and line 127 runs `bun run eval:run`. That script is `bun eval/runner/multi-adapter.ts` (package.json:13), which always runs VectorOnlyAdapter and HybridNoGraphAdapter; eval/runner/adapters/vector.ts:33 `import { embed, embedBatch } from 'gbrain/embedding'` calls the real OpenAI API. The repo's own RUNBOOK contradicts the README: eval/RUNBOOK.md:7-17 "OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is missing — The embedding adapter (vector) ... calls the OpenAI API. You need an API key. ... bun run eval:run". Line 127 also mislabels eval:run as "the full retrieval + behavior suite" — the behavior cats (identity, temporal, adversarial, multimodal, cat34) live in `eval:brainbench` (eval/runner/all.ts), not multi-adapter.ts.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the command to the actually-offline path (e.g. `bun run eval:run -- --adapter=gbrain` and `--adapter=grep-only`, which are keyless) or drop the 'no API keys, fully offline' claim; point 'behavior suite' at `bun run eval:brainbench`.
findings.status_note: keys note scoped honestly

findings.verifier_note: Line 181 (repeated at 232 and 268) claims a committed ~150MB SQLite cache at eval/data/longmemeval/embed-cache/. git ls-files shows that directory contains only README.md, whose first line is '# Embedding cache — content-addressed (NOT committed)' and which says caches land at gitignored eval/reports/longmemeval/embed-cache/ (~700MB for the full _s split). eval/runner/longmemeval.ts:110 defaults cacheDir to eval/reports/longmemeval/embed-cache with a comment (lines 104-109) saying exactly that. A fresh clone pays the ~$2 cold-embed cost the report says is prepaid.
findings.title: Report claims warm embedding cache 'ships committed' — it is not committed and the path is wrong
findings.evidence: Line 181: "The cache file lives at `eval/data/longmemeval/embed-cache/` and ships committed in this repo (~150MB SQLite). On clone you get a warm cache; runs are sub-1-min..." (repeated at lines 232 and 268). The directory contains only README.md, whose first line is "# Embedding cache — content-addressed (NOT committed)" and which says cache files land at `eval/reports/longmemeval/embed-cache/` (gitignored) and the full `_s` cache is ~700MB, "too big for plain git". The runner agrees: eval/runner/longmemeval.ts:110 defaults cacheDir to `eval/reports/longmemeval/embed-cache` with the comment "gitignored ... ~700MB, too big to commit". A fresh clone pays the ~$2 cold-embed cost the report says is already paid.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite §8/§10/§12 to match reality: cache is NOT committed, lives under gitignored eval/reports/longmemeval/embed-cache/, is ~700MB for the full split, and first runs cost ~$2; keep the 'copy the sqlite via scp/s3' sharing instructions from the cache README.
findings.status_note: Report's three cache claims (§8, §10, §12) rewritten: cache is NOT committed, lives at gitignored eval/reports/longmemeval/embed-cache/ (~700MB full _s), fresh clone pays ~$2 once; scp/s3 sharing pointer kept. ERRATUM block untouched.

findings.verifier_note: README.md:82-83 defines 'shipping' as runs-in-CI-and-gates-releases; all 11 rows (lines 87-97) are 'shipping'. git ls-files shows no .github/ or any CI config in this repo, and gbrain's own .github/workflows never reference gbrain-evals (they run gbrain-internal eval tests only). eval/runner/all.ts marks Cat 5 (lines 78-84), Cat 8 (97-103), Cat 9 (104-110) as kind:'programmatic' — recorded but never executed (header comment lines 21-25). Nuance that doesn't rescue the claim: test/eval/cat5.test.ts and cat8-cat9.test.ts exist but use stubbed LLM clients (harness unit tests, not the accuracy>0.90 / 80%-pass benchmark rows), and eval/data/gold/citations.json is actually committed yet still unwired in all.ts.
findings.title: 'Shipping means it runs in CI and gates releases' — repo has no CI, and 3 listed rows are skipped by the master runner
findings.evidence: README.md:82-83: "Each row is a real test with a committed pass/fail threshold. 'Shipping' means it runs in CI and gates releases." — all 11 rows are marked "shipping". The repo contains no CI configuration at all (no .github/, no workflow files in `git ls-files`). Worse, three of the rows never execute in the committed pipeline: eval/runner/all.ts marks Cat 5 Provenance (line 79-83, "needs a claim catalog"), Cat 8 Skills (line 98-102) and Cat 9 Workflows (line 105-109) as kind:'programmatic', which the runner reports without executing — yet README rows "Provenance | accuracy > 0.90 | shipping", "Skills | all > 0.90 | shipping", "Workflows | 80% pass | shipping" present them as gating tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the CI workflow that runs `bun run eval:brainbench` + `bun test test/eval/` and wire Cats 5/8/9 with their catalogs, or change the Status column to reflect reality (e.g. 'harness only, run manually' for 5/8/9) and drop the 'runs in CI and gates releases' definition.
findings.status_note: CI claim matches the actual workflow

findings.verifier_note: README.md:170-171 and 6-7 claim reproduce-from-commit-hash; package.json:30 pins gbrain to 'github:garrytan/gbrain#master' (floating). Worse, .gitignore excludes bun.lockb and bun.lock, so no lockfile freezes the SHA either — `git checkout <sha> && bun install` fetches today's gbrain master. The LongMemEval scorecard pins gbrain v0.28.8 (report lines 4, 277) while gbrain master is now 0.47.6.0 (/home/vercel-sandbox/gbrain/VERSION). eval/README.md:90-93 (Path 1) tells the user to `git checkout <commit-sha>` for 'the specific gbrain commit referenced in the scorecard' inside gbrain-evals, which cannot pin the gbrain library without a bun-link step it never mentions.
findings.title: Reproduce-from-commit claim broken: gbrain dependency floats on #master, not a pinned SHA
findings.evidence: README.md:170-171: "**Reproduce a result:** every scorecard names the commit it ran on. `git checkout <sha> && bun run eval:run`." and line 6-7 "can be reproduced from a commit hash". But package.json:30 pins `"gbrain": "github:garrytan/gbrain#master"` — a floating branch. Checking out an old gbrain-evals SHA and running `bun install` fetches today's gbrain master, not the version the scorecard measured (e.g. the LongMemEval report pins gbrain v0.28.8; current master is v0.47.6.0). eval/README.md:89-92 (Path 1) has the same flaw: it says to check out "the specific gbrain commit referenced in the scorecard" inside this repo, which does nothing without a bun-link step.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the gbrain dependency to a commit SHA per release (github:garrytan/gbrain#<sha>) and bump it deliberately, or document the required `bun link` of a gbrain checkout at the scorecard's pinned SHA as part of the reproduction steps.
findings.status_note: pin + frozen lockfile + pre-pin caveat

findings.verifier_note: eval/README.md:129-131 claims P@5/R@5 cover '145 canonical from _facts, 80 tier-5 + tier-5.5'. multi-adapter.ts builds queries exclusively from _facts in buildQueries() (lines 66-130: attendees/employees/founders/investors/advisors) and imports no tier files. Repo-wide grep: tier5-fuzzy.ts (30) and tier5_5-synthetic.ts (50) are imported only by eval/runner/queries/index.ts, which is imported only by eval/cli/query-validate.ts (validation CLI, no scoring). The published scorecard (eval/README.md:138-148) therefore covers only the canonical set.
findings.title: Methodology claims metrics include '80 tier-5 + tier-5.5' queries that no scorer ever runs
findings.evidence: eval/README.md:129-131: "**Metrics:** P@5 and R@5 on relational queries (145 canonical from `_facts`, 80 tier-5 + tier-5.5)." The scorer behind `bun run eval:run` (eval/runner/multi-adapter.ts) builds queries exclusively from `_facts` via buildQueries() (lines 66-130) and never imports the tier files. findings.verifier_note: Lines 9-13 report 0.150 kta failure, line 81 'n (gold turns) 146 kta', line 98 '9/146', lines 102-104 'the know-to-ask failure rate is 0.150 on every seam — those 9 misses'. 9/146 = 0.062; the actual formula at gbrain/src/eval/brainbench/metrics/know-to-ask.ts:57 is missed/shouldRetrieve while gold_total = shouldRetrieve + quiet (line 54). The numbers only reconcile with shouldRetrieve=60, quiet=86 (9/60 = 0.150; claude-code's 2 false fires / 86 = 0.023 matching line 12), and the 60/86 split appears nowhere in the doc, leaving the published tables internally inconsistent as claimed.
findings.title: know-to-ask failure rate 0.150 cannot be reconciled with the printed 9/146 — denominator never stated
findings.evidence: Line 9-13 report know-to-ask failure 0.150 against "n (gold turns) 146 kta" (line 81), and line 98 prints "kta failed/gold 9/146"; but 9/146 = 0.062 and 0.150 x 146 = 22. The actual formula (gbrain src/eval/brainbench/metrics/know-to-ask.ts:57) is `missed / shouldRetrieve` where shouldRetrieve is only the should-retrieve subset (9/60 = 0.150) while gold_total = shouldRetrieve + quiet = 146. The doc never states the 60-turn denominator, so its own tables look internally inconsistent (line 103 "the know-to-ask failure rate is 0.150 on every seam — those 9 misses").
findings.suggested_fix: State the split explicitly in the Results/Methodology sections: 146 kta gold turns = 60 should-retrieve + 86 stay-silent; failure rate = misses/60, false-fire rate = fires/86, and failed/gold counts sum both.
findings.status_note: Added the missing denominator split in the per-suite breakdown (146 kta gold = 60 should-retrieve + 86 stay-silent; 9/60=0.150; claude-code 2/86=0.023; failed/gold sums both, explaining 11/146) plus a one-line formula note in Methodology, citing gbrain's know-to-ask.ts formula.

critic_gaps.area: eval/data/gold/ template layer — assigned to no unit as data; 4 of 7 gold files have zero consumers and all 7 are single-example stubs

critic_gaps.area: eval/CONTRIBUTING.md + eval/CREDITS.md — uncovered; documented contribution path is broken

critic_gaps.area: Root config files: tsconfig.json, VERSION, LICENSE, .gitignore — uncovered

VERSION (0.2.0) vs CHANGELOG consistency was not explicitly asserted by the docs unit.
critic_gaps.suggested_check: Extend tsconfig include to scripts/, decide whether results/ should be gitignored like eval/reports/, and add a test that VERSION matches the latest CHANGELOG entry.

critic_overall: Coverage of eval/runner, test/eval, the current-generation docs, and the gbrain import surface was thorough — the 17 units collectively touched every .ts/.sh source file under eval/ and test/. The uncovered surface is concentrated in artifacts and periphery: the committed results/shootout/ run outputs (which encode two verifiable defects nobody reported: phase2.sh never passes --cell so receipts ship with cell:null, and the committed shootout is 1 of 7 cells with no doc referencing it), 11 of 16 published benchmark reports (including two already known-stale from other units' code findings), the shootout operator runbook, the vendored PrecisionMemBench fixtures whose byte-for-byte upstream claim was never diffed, the eval/data/gold template layer (all 7 files are single-example stubs, 4 with zero consumers, despite _comments claiming real planted content), and the contribution docs whose referenced submission paths (.github PR template, eval/external-authors/) do not exist. Cross-cutting checks no unit performed: recall/precision exist in at least 7 divergent implementations so same-named columns across published pages are different statistics; the gbrain_version:'unknown' provenance bug spans all 17 runners cat18-cat33 (cats22-25's auditor missed their four); and env-var set-vs-read analysis found GBRAIN_SEARCH_MODE set but read nowhere, GBRAIN_REPO/GBRAIN_SRC naming drift for the same concept, and ~37 of ~39 tuning knobs undocumented in any doc, undermining run reconstructability.
